items.title: [Bug] MiMoV2MTP silently drops FP8 KV cache scales and every draft layer falls back to scale 1.0
items.author: GowayLee
items.body_excerpt:
## Describe the bug

When a MiMo-V2 checkpoint with speculative MTP carries FP8 KV cache scales, `MiMoV2MTP.load_weights` drops them under every naming family, the scale parameters keep their -1.0 sentinel, and `process_weights_after_loading` resets both to 1.0. Every draft layer then quantizes and dequantizes its cache with a unit scale, outputs stay finite, and the only visible trace is a startup warning that points at the checkpoint.

```python
# vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py, current main
elif layer.k_scale < 0.0 and layer.v_scale < 0.0:
    # If no scales were loaded (both scales are invalid negative
    # values), use the default value of 1.0
    k_scale = 1.0
    v_scale = 1.0
```

The fallback logs "Using KV cache scaling factor 1.0 for fp8_e4m3. If this is unintended, verify that k/v_scale scaling factors are properly set in the checkpoint." A checkpoint that does carry the scales still triggers it, because the loss happens inside the loader.

Three scale namings are affected. llm-compressor stores the scales under the fused projection name, for example `model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale` (the layout reported in #25047). ModelOpt stores them per projection, for example `model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale`. The deprecated single `.kv_scale` tensor is lost as well, while the model registers the scales at `self_attn.attn.k_scale` and `self_attn.attn.v_scale`.

### Mechanism

The fused-projection branch runs before the params lookup. It pairs an fp8 `qkv_proj.weight` with its `weight_scale_inv`, loads a non-fp8 fused weight when the name is registered, and ends with a bare `continue` for everything else.

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_mtp.py, current main
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    is_fp8_weight = (
        name.endswith("qkv_proj.weight")
        and loaded_weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
    )
    is_fp8_scale = name.endswith("qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv")
    if is_fp8_weight or is_fp8_scale:
        ...pair and shard...
    elif name in params_dict:
        ...load...
    continue
```

A fused scale name matches neither guard and is not registered, so it reaches the trailing `continue` without a log. The per-projection name survives to the stacked mapping, which rewrites `k_proj.k_scale` into `qkv_proj.k_scale`; the scales live on `self_attn.attn`, so that name is not registered either, and the name falls through the loop. The deprecated name falls straight through. All three paths end in a `continue` with no log.

The main model handles the scales in both variants. The Flash variant calls `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` in its hand-written loader, and the Pro variant loads through `AutoWeightsLoader`, which applies the cache-scale mapper automatically. The MTP draft model is the gap.

#25047 fixed this class of loss for the main models and #35656 landed the mechanism. #43167 then centralized the per-model boilerplate into `quant_config.get_cache_scale_mapper()` applied by `AutoWeightsLoader`, migrating every model file that carried the boilerplate. `MiMoV2MTP` entered in #40967 and #41905 without any scale handling, so the cleanup had nothing to remove and the draft model kept dropping the scales. `MiMoV2OmniMTP` inherits the same loader and is affected as well.

## Measured evidence

Two independent runs establish the behavior. The verification harness runs `MiMoV2MTP.load_weights` verbatim from commit `41cffa9af0` on CPU with a synthetic checkpoint (`k_scale=12.5`, `v_scale=0.03125` under each naming) and continues into the verbatim `process_weights_after_loading`. All 6 combinations (3 namings x unmodified and fixed) behaved as predicted; the unmodified loader dropped the scales with effective 1.0 / 1.0 and reproduced the startup warning, and the fixed loader landed `12.5` / `0.03125` under all three namings. The function has since gained the fused fp8 pairing path from #58142 and #57508, which does not touch the scale-drop paths. The regression test attached to the PR runs the current loader from main `33138259` with the real `Fp8Config` mapper, and its three scale cases fail on main and pass with the fix. In both runs the control weights (the fused `qkv_proj.weight` and `embed_tokens`) load normally, so the drops are specific to the scale names, and the deprecated single `kv_scale` lands on `k_scale` with the `v` copy duplicated in `process_weights_after_loading`, as for every other model.

## To Reproduce

The loop below mirrors the fused-projection branch, the stacked rewrite, and the params lookup of `MiMoV2MTP.load_weights`, including the continue-on-miss semantics, and needs no vllm import.

```python
params_dict = {
    "model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight",  # what the model registers
    "model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.attn.k_scale",
    "model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.attn.v_scale",
}
stacked_params_mapping = [
    ("gate_up_proj", "gate_proj", 0),
    ("gate_up_proj", "up_proj", 1),
    ("qkv_proj", "q_proj", "q"),
    ("qkv_proj", "k_proj", "k"),
    ("qkv_proj", "v_proj", "v"),
]
fixtures = [
    ("model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight", "bf16"),          # control
    ("model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight", "float8_e4m3fn"),  # fp8 pairing path
    ("model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale", "fp32"),          # llm-compressor fused
    ("model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale", "fp32"),            # ModelOpt per-projection
    ("model.mtp.layers.0.self_attn.kv_scale", "fp32"),                  # deprecated
]

for ckpt_name, dtype in fixtures:
    name = ckpt_name
    if "qkv_proj" in name:
        is_fp8_weight = name.endswith("qkv_proj.weight") and dtype == "float8_e4m3fn"
        is_fp8_scale = name.endswith("qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv")
        if is_fp8_weight or is_fp8_scale:
            print(f"pairing {ckpt_name}  (fused fp8 path)")
        elif name in params_dict:
            print(f"loaded  {ckpt_name}")
        else:

items.title: [Feature] Implement Image Number Limitation for Image Processors
items.author: JustinTong0323
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [ ] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

At present, there is no limitation on the number of images during the processing of mm data. It is necessary to impose such a limitation to prevent potential OOM and other problems.

(When using fast image processor, the GPU memory usage is roughly **1GiB** for each **4K** image)

### Related resources

Implementation Steps:
1. Define a constant, such as `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION = 5`, for each processor.
2. Modify the `baseprocessor` to utilize this constant for request validation.
3. Incorporate a server argument to enable modification of this numerical value.

In case you lack familiarity with the mm data processing pipeline, it is advisable to first refer to [here](https://github.com/zhaochenyang20/Awesome-ML-SYS-Tutorial/blob/main/sglang/code-walk-through/multimodal_request_lifecycle.md)

items.title: [Misc]: CMake Clean-up / Refactor Tasks
items.author: LucasWilkinson
items.body_excerpt:
In an effort to make the CMake more readable, stable and easy to use we have a few tasks we'd like to work on, creating a GitHub issue here to track that progress, some planned changes/investigations:

- [ ] Rename `define_gpu_extension_target`, currently this is used for CPU extensions too so the name is now misleading
- [ ] Add a CI test of local builds, i.e. `pip install -e .`
- [ ]  Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8845), currently if there is a `+PTX` in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` this will be ignored. We should warn when this is the case. Alternatively we can add support for PTX builds although this is generally not desirable since PTX increases the wheel size by quite a bit (PTX is larger than SASS), and we already build for all currently supported arches.
- [ ]  Have vllm-flash-attn use [ExternalProject](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/ExternalProject.html) currently vllm-flash-attn uses the parent CMake scope which creates many footguns since it is in a separate repo, using `ExternalProject` will mean that the vllm-flash-attn will be run in a separate CMake scope/process
  - [ ] It might be even better to revert to the FlashMLA approach, where CMake code lives in vllm.
- [ ] Look into removing early returns in CMakeLists.txt (potentially move backends into its own files)
- [ ] Potential build both C++ and CUDA extensions when building for CUDA and using torch dispatcher to dispatch between the two, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8424

items.title: [Bug] --enable-linear-replayssm forces no_buffer, which degrades mamba prefix caching and inflates TTFT up to 4.7x
items.author: davidli1515
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Describe the bug `--enable-linear-replayssm` requires `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer`. That strategy stores the mamba checkpoint at a radix-tree depth later requests cannot reach, so prefix reuse collapses and TTFT rises sharply on any workload with a shared prefix. ### Measured Qwen3.8-27B, 1×H200, TP=1, `sglang.benchmark.serving`, `--request-rate 8 --max-concurrency 48`. Both arms use `--disable-overlap-schedule`, because `no_buffer` asserts against the overlap scheduler; holding it fixed keeps the cache strategy the only variable. - **default** = `extra_buffer`, no ReplaySSM (what most users run today) - **replayssm** = `--enable-linear-replayssm`, which forces `no_buffer` | workload | arm | prefix cache hit | out tok/s | TTFT mean | TTFT p99 | E2E mean | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **rag**
2048-tok shared prefix
(8 groups × 32) | default | **88.2%** | 509.6 | 226.4 ms | 1788.2 ms | 2164.7 ms | | | replayssm | **65.9%** | 508.7 | **1062.6 ms** | **4116.2 ms** | 3876.4 ms | | | | | −0.2% | **+369%** | **+130%** | **+79%** | | **fewshot**
512-tok shared prefix
(32 groups × 8) | default | **62.2%** | 510.1 | 83.0 ms | 261.5 ms | 1959.6 ms | | | replayssm | **0.0%** | 508.9 | **159.0 ms** | **622.3 ms** | 3048.2 ms | | | | | −0.2% | **+92%** | **+138%** | **+56%** | | **sharegpt**
real conversations,
little cross-request sharing | default | 0.7% | 1136.7 | 95.9 ms | 476.6 ms | 7145.5 ms | | | replayssm | 0.0% | 1162.6 | 97.0 ms | 477.8 ms | 6929.3 ms | | | | | +2.3% | +1.1% | +0.3% | −3.0% | Hit rate is `cached / (cached + new)` summed over the server's own `Prefill batch ... #cached-token:` lines. ShareGPT is the control: consecutive requests share almost nothing, both arms sit near a 0% hit rate, and the two configurations become indistinguishable. The gap only appears where prefixes are actually shared, which is what confirms the regression comes from prefix reuse and not from some other effect of the flag. ### Why output throughput is flat Throughput is unchanged in every row, but that is a property of the load point, not evidence that the regression is free. At `--request-rate 8` with 64-token outputs the offered rate is ~512 tok/s for the two `generated-shared-prefix` runs, and measured throughput is 508–510: the server delivered exactly what arrived, so throughput was pinned by the arrival rate rather than by the server. The ShareGPT rows in the same table reach 1137–1163 tok/s on the same server, which alone shows capacity is more than twice what the shared-prefix runs asked for. Below saturation the extra prefill work has nowhere to go except queueing delay, so it lands entirely on **TTFT and E2E**. At saturation it would convert into a throughput loss instead. ### Mechanism `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba_component.py:529-533` chooses the tree depth the mamba checkpoint is attached to: ```python if self.cache.enable_mamba_extra_buffer: cache_len = req.mamba_last_track_seqlen # a boundary reached DURING the prompt else: # no_buffer cache_len = token_ids_len # prompt + this request's OWN generated tokens ``` Requests share a *prompt*; their generated continuations differ. Under `no_buffer` the checkpoint sits past the end of the prompt, so a follow-up request walks the tree only to the end of its own prompt, lands on a node that carries no mamba value, and the mamba match validator rejects it. Because a forward pass resumes from a single position for all layers, a missing mamba anchor also discards the KV hit. Instrumenting the match path on a 601-token prompt whose predecessor stored 608: ``` insert: finished=True token_ids_len=608 -> cache_len=608 match: full_kv_hit_length=600 mamba_boundary=0 branching_seqlen=576 result: #new-token: 601, #cached-token: 0 ``` KV alone could have reused 600 tokens. It reused none. Severity scales with shared-prefix length: with a 512-token prefix the hit rate goes to exactly 0%, while with a 2048-token prefix it only falls to 65.9% — long prefixes contain enough grid-aligned positions that some reuse survives. ### Is this intended? `no_buffer` avoids the extra ping-pong buffer, so trading memory for reduced cross-request reuse could be deliberate. If it is, could the trade-off be documented and could the `--enable-linear-replayssm` guard mention it? Users enabling ReplaySSM for decode bandwidth are unlikely to expect a TTFT regression of this size. If it is not intended, the guard's own comment points at the cause — `donate_mamba_ping_pong_slot` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1454`) never resets `replayssm_write_pos`, unlike `MambaPool.copy_from` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:997`), which is why `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:6357` refuses `extra_buffer`: > the extra_buffer ping-pong donation path is not yet supported (follow-up) I have a candidate fix along those lines (two edits, ~7 lines) that restores the hit rate and TTFT to the default arm's numbers with GSM8K accuracy parity over 1319 questions and a clean 6.5-hour soak. I will open it as a PR referencing this issue. ### Scope of verification - Reproduced on **UnifiedRadixCache** (`Init Unified Radix Cache. Components: (FULL, MAMBA). Tree Core: UnifiedTreeCore`). The legacy `MambaRadixCache` has the same code shape (`mamba_component.py` notes it "Mirrors `MambaRadixCache.cache_finished_req`") but I have not tested

items.title: [Bug]: Wrong timestamps if audio > 30s
items.author: dr75
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment


NA

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Segment level timestamps are incrementally offset by ~0.5s per segment.**

When transcribing long audio with vLLM Whisper, segment-level timestamps are increasingly inaccurate. Chunking uses by default a 1s window to find low-energy (quiet) regions for splitting, so the next chunk may start up to 1s earlier than the nominal chunk length. This offset is not compensated for when generating segment timestamps, resulting in an average delay of ~0.5s per segment, which accumulates (e.g., 5s after 10 segments).

Clients can workaround by subtracting 0.5s per segment, but that's obviously not accurate.

Also, the [related documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e83b7e379c11bf136c1b96bc6a67b6d2207cfde4/docs/contributing/model/transcription.md#audio-preprocessing-and-chunking) is not correct: there are no overlapping chunks, but just a window for searching the best split point. Maybe this confusion is the cause of the issue.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

We currently have the following MoE "oracles", which select the right MoE kernel for each model

- fp8
- nvfp4

class MoEKernelOracle(ABC)
 ...

class Fp8MoEKernelOracle(MoEOracle):
 ...

and so on and so forth


### Alternatives

just use conventions. this is a bad idea due to drift and duplicated code

items.title: [RFC]: KVarN: a calibration-free, variance-normalized sub-8-bit KV-cache quantization backend
items.author: philippebich
items.body_excerpt:
### Motivation.

KV cache is the dominant memory cost for long-context and high-concurrency serving. vLLM already supports fp8 KV cache (~2x capacity) and, as of [#38479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38479), a sub-4-bit rotation-based backend (**TurboQuant**). But sub-4-bit KV quantization is still rarely turned on in production, for one reason: **it costs throughput and accuracy.**

As vLLM's own [TurboQuant blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-05-11-turboquant) reports, existing sub-4-bit methods buy 2.3 to 3.7x capacity but give up **40 to 52% of throughput**, and aggressive low-bit quant also tends to cost accuracy. Losing both speed and quality is why the feature stays off.

**KVarN** ([arXiv:2606.03458](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03458)) is a variance-normalized KV-cache quantization scheme built to keep all three at once: capacity, throughput, and accuracy.

- **~3.2 to 3.4x measured KV-cache capacity** at int4-K / int2-V.
- **Throughput at or above FP16/baseline in the memory-bound regime**, *uniquely* among KV-quant backends (measured +9% at 14B, rising to +18% at ~106B), not the throughput regression every other sub-4-bit method pays.
- **FP16-level accuracy**, calibration-free, no model changes, one flag (measured lossless on Qwen3-14B/30B and GLM-4.5-Air).

It also covers models TurboQuant cannot: it supports MLA, and it runs on hybrid and sliding-window models. TurboQuant supports full-attention and uniform sliding-window only.

Mechanism in one line: a Sinkhorn variance-normalizing rotation equalizes per-channel scale before scalar int4/int2 quantization, with a small fp16 outlier/sink pool, which is what preserves accuracy without calibration. (Full method in the paper.)

### Proposed Change.

Add KVarN as a **native vLLM attention backend selected via `--kv-cache-dtype`**, fully transparent (pass-through) for every non-KVarN dtype.

- **New backend** for the dense path (`KVarNAttentionBackend`) plus an MLA latent-quant path on the FlashMLA backend.
- **KV-cache dtypes / presets** (e.g. `kvarn_k4v2_g128`, `kvarn_k4v2_g64`): one flag, no calibration, no checkpoint changes.
- **Kernels are Triton, JIT-compiled at runtime**: store, dequant, split-K decode, and the Sinkhorn normalization. No C++/CUDA build step; works on the upstream precompiled wheel (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`).
- **Coverage:** head sizes 64 / 128 / 256; fp16 and bf16 activations; GQA; full-attention, sliding-window, and hybrid models; MLA (validated on the dense FlashMLA latent path, with CUDA-graph capture).
- **Integration footprint is small and isolated:** a handful of registration/routing edits (KV-cache dtype registry, backend selector, cache config) plus the self-contained backend, ops, and a `quantization/kvarn/` config/Sinkhorn module. The feature touches no existing backend's behavior.

### Evidence
Measured on the same box, vLLM main with the merged TurboQuant backend present. All comparisons are apples-to-apples: identical prompts/weights, CUDA graphs on, the same `gpu_memory_utilization` for every config, so the only variable is `--kv-cache-dtype`. Headline configs are the two we propose to ship: `kvarn_k4v2_g128` (4-bit K / 2-bit V, ~3 bits avg) and `kvarn_k4v4_g128` (4-bit K / 4-bit V). The bit-matched TurboQuant rival to k4v2 is `turboquant_3bit_nc` (3 bits).

**1. Throughput, memory-bound regime** (the regime the [blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-04-22-fp8-kvcache) measures: distinct long prompts, prefix-caching off, concurrency high enough to pressure the KV cache). Qwen3-14B, 256 distinct prompts, GMU 0.85, aggregate serving throughput (tok/s):

| context | FP16 | **KVarN k4v2** | KVarN k4v4 | TQ-4bit | TQ-3bit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6K | 475.7 | **520.4 (+9.4%)** | 485.5 (+2%) | 405.8 (-15%) | 356.3 (-25%) |
| 12K | 238.5 | **258.7 (+8.5%)** | 227.9 | 202.2 (-15%) | 179.7 (-25%) |

**KVarN is the only KV-quant backend that sustains throughput above FP16.** Every TurboQuant variant lands below it (-15 to -25% here at 14B), matching the throughput tax vLLM's own blogs document for TurboQuant up to 52% in the [TurboQuant blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-05-11-turboquant)). Versus the bit-matched TQ-3bit, KVarN k4v2 is **1.44x** the throughput. The mechanism: TQ's dequant is expensive enough that its capacity gain nets negative vs FP16; KVarN's is cheap enough that its capacity gain nets positive. In the non-memory-bound regime (short shared prefixes) FP16 is fastest, as expected, and the blog agrees KV quant is for the memory-bound case.

**The lead grows with scale.** On **GLM-4.5-Air-FP8** (~106B GQA MoE, fp8 weights, TP=2, 12K ctx, B=256), on top of the fp8-weight baseline KVarN k4v2 adds throughput and capacity while TurboQuant subtracts a third of it:

| | baseline (fp8 wts + 16-bit KV) | **KVarN k4v2** | KVarN k4v4 | TQ-4bit | TQ-3bit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| throughput (tok/s) | 258.9 | **304.5 (+17.6%)** | 265.9 | 177.6 (-31%) | 153.2 (-41%) |
| KV capacity | 1.0x | **3.2x** | 2.5x | 3.1x | 3.7x |

KVarN k4v2 is **2.0x TQ-3bit / 1.7x TQ-4bit** throughput here; TurboQuant's -31/-41% lands in the blog's own 40 to 52% loss range. The bigger, TP-sharded model is less weight-bound, so the KV-path win rises from +9% (14B) to +17.6% (~106B).

**2. Accuracy, AIME-2026 avg@3** (Qwen3-30B-A3B, the blog's own model;):

| FP16 | **KVarN k4v2** | **KVarN k4v4** | TQ-4bit | TQ-3bit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 72.2 | **72.2 (lossless)** | **72.2 (lossless)** | 71.1 (-1.1) | **57.8 (-14.4)** |

Both shipped presets are **FP16-lossless**. At the matched ~3-bit budget, TQ-3bit drops **14.4 points** while KVarN k4v2 loses nothing: KVarN spends its bits on a 4-bit K plus a small fp16 outlier pool instead of crushing everything to 3 bits. (KVarN is also lossless on Qwen3-14B: 73.3 vs FP16 73.4.)

This holds at scale: on **GLM-4.5-Air-FP8** (~106B, TP=2) KVarN k4v2 matches the fp8-weight baseline seed-for-seed (78.9 vs 78.9), while TQ-3bit drops to 72.2 (-6.7) and runs ~3x slower on the reas

items.title: [Performance]: FlashAttention backend rebuilds KV-cache views on every call (+~21 µs CPU/layer since #44455)
items.author: rrranlyu
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Cache the (canonicalized) views on the impl and reuse them while the same `kv_cache` tensor is passed in. On v0.30, a local patch doing this cuts TTFT p50 by 12–16%, and the outputs match an fp32 reference with no numerical change:


```python
# FlashAttentionImpl
def _get_kv_views(self, kv_cache, canonicalize: bool):
    c = self._kv_view_cache
    if c is None or c[0] is not kv_cache:
        k, v = kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(self.head_size, dim=-1)
        ck, cv = canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides(k), canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides(v)
        c = self._kv_view_cache = (kv_cache, k, v, ck, cv)
    return (c[3], c[4]) if canonicalize else (c[1], c[2])
```

Notes:
- The identity check matters. `profile_cudagraph_memory` first binds a minimal KV cache (`_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling`), runs attention on it, frees it, and then allocates the real one. A cache keyed only on the first call would keep pointing at freed memory.
- There is precedent for this: `TritonAttentionImpl` already caches KV-scale views in `_k_scale_cache` / `_v_scale_cache` ([triton_attn.py#L383-L440](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py#L383-L440)), and `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` clears them. The FA view cache could be cleared in the same place. It should also be kept per impl, not in a module-level dict, so that the replaced tensor is not kept alive.
- Hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.5) only get this cost on their `full_attention` layers.

I'm happy to open a PR.


### Report of performance regression

Since #44455 (KV-cache layout refactor, v0.26), `FlashAttentionImpl` derives the K/V cache views on every call:

- `forward`: `kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(self.head_size, dim=-1)`, then `canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides` on both views ([flash_attn.py#L1232-L1250 @ v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L1232-L1250))
- `do_kv_cache_update`: the same `transpose(1, 2).split(...)` ([flash_attn.py#L1454 @ v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L1454))

Before #44455 this was a single `kv_cache.unbind(1)` ([v0.25.0#L816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.25.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L816)). The code is unchanged on current `main`.

These views depend only on the per-layer `kv_cache` tensor's storage, shape and strides. That tensor is fixed once the KV cache is allocated. The views are recomputed per layer per step anyway, and the slots each step touches come in separately via `slot_mapping` / `block_table`.

Under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, attention for prefill / mixed batches runs eagerly, so this is host time on the critical path for short prefills.

| per attention call (profiler, H100) | v0.25 | v0.26 |
|---|---|---|
| K/V view ops | `unbind` + 2× `select`: 11.6 µs | `transpose` + `split` + 2× `narrow`: 17.0 µs |
| `unified_attention_with_output` total | 134.1 µs | 155.2 µs (+21) |

For a 64-layer model that is about +1.35 ms per prefill step. On 8×H100 (TP=8), with short prompts and `max_tokens=1`, TTFT p50 went up 1–3.5 ms from 0.25 to 0.26. Only the FA backend is affected; FlashInfer is not.


### Misc discussion on performance

_No response_

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

```text
vLLM 0.30.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0), torch 2.13.0+cu130
8x H100 80GB (TP=8), attention backend FLASH_ATTN (FA3)
--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (default)
```

items.title: [Bug] Native connector worker death leaves L2 adapter pending maps and L1 read locks stuck
items.author: Writtic
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**

Please label as `bug`.

**Summary**

`ConnectorBase`'s worker loop can exit with requests still queued, and nothing tells the Python side. Every `future_id` submitted to that worker then sits in `NativeConnectorL2Adapter`'s pending maps for the life of the process, and for stores it also pins the L1 read locks the in-flight task holds.

Raised in review on #4211 by @maobaolong. Filing it separately as agreed there, since the fix belongs to the C++ completion contract rather than the adapter.

**Details**

The adapter pairs every insert into `_pending_ops`, `_pending_store_sizes`, and `_pending_store_tasks` with a removal: the submit failure path cleans up its own entries, and the demux thread pops all three when a completion arrives. The maps grow without bound only when a submitted `future_id` never produces a completion.

`worker_loop_for_queue` in `csrc/storage_backends/connector_base.h` has two such paths:

1. `create_connection()` throws before the request loop starts. The outer `catch` prints to stderr and the worker returns, leaving its queue undrained.
2. A non-`std::exception` escapes the per-tile `catch (const std::exception&)`, unwinds to `catch (...)`, and kills the worker. That tile never reaches `handle_tile_completion`.

Both report through `fprintf(stderr, ...)` instead of the logger, so a dead worker is easy to miss.

For stores the cost is larger than dict growth. `StoreController` records `read_locked_keys` per in-flight task and releases them on completion, so a task that never completes holds L1 read locks until the process exits and those chunks cannot be evicted.

**Expected Outcome / Goal**

Every submitted `future_id` gets exactly one completion, including when its worker dies. Options worth discussing:

- On worker exit, drain the queue and push a failed `Completion` for each pending request.
- Widen the per-tile catch to `catch (...)`, so an unknown exception fails one tile instead of the worker.
- Report worker death through the logger and a metric, not only stderr.

**Actual Outcome**

The maps grow without bound and the store task never completes. #4211 adds `lmcache_mp.l2_adapter_pending_entries`, a gauge over the three maps per adapter, which makes this visible: a series that keeps climbing without returning to zero is this leak.

items.title: [Bug] fs L2 adapter: every store fails at os.open() in _write_with_odirect when use_odirect=true
items.author: h1manshu23
items.body_excerpt:
**Describe the bug**
With the `fs` L2 adapter and `use_odirect: true`, **every** chunk store fails. `FSL2Adapter._write_with_odirect` raises at the `os.open()` call, and each store is logged as failed:

```
[2026-07-31 12:39:27,361] LMCache ERROR: FSL2Adapter failed to store
/mnt/nvme0/-SEP-data-medium-SEP-text-generation-models-SEP-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic-SEP-@0x01000100@1@246ba704d24a7690450504e0a607656c195b4e247501896d103d7d293f9b63dc.data
(fs_l2_adapter.py:629:lmcache.v1.distributed.l2_adapters.fs_l2_adapter)
```

Nothing is ever persisted to L2, so the disk tier is effectively dead while the server continues running and reporting no fatal error.

**This is not an unsupported-storage case.** `base_path=/mnt/nvme0` is a real block-backed filesystem on a 4-device NVMe RAID0 array:

```
md0 : active raid0 nvme3n2[3] nvme2n2[2] nvme1n2[1] nvme4n2[0]
```

Two distinct problems here:

1. **The failure itself.** O_DIRECT should be usable on this mount. Whatever LMCache passes to `os.open()` — flag combination, mode, or path — is being rejected on a filesystem/device stack that otherwise accepts direct I/O.
2. **The failure is undiagnosable and unrecoverable.** The log line prints the target path but not the underlying `OSError`/errno, so there's no way to tell EINVAL from EACCES from ENOENT without reading LMCache's source. And there is no fallback: rather than degrading to buffered I/O or refusing at startup, the adapter fails silently-but-endlessly, once per chunk, for the lifetime of the server.

Note the failure is at **`os.open()`**, not at the write — so this is not an O_DIRECT buffer/offset/length alignment issue, which would surface later in `_write_with_odirect`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `base_path` sits on a 4× NVMe md RAID0 (512k chunk) mounted at `/mnt/nvme0`.

2. Start the LMCache server with the `fs` L2 adapter and O_DIRECT enabled:

```bash
lmcache server --host localhost --port 9000 \
  --l1-size-gb 128 --eviction-policy LRU --chunk-size 256 \
  --l2-adapter '{"type": "fs", "base_path": "/mnt/nvme0", "use_odirect": true, "num_workers": 32}' \
  --http-port 8081
```

3. Start vLLM against it on a single GPU:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve /path/to/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic/ \
  --port 9001 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.port":9000}}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 12
```

4. Send any request. Every L2 store fails with the traceback below; `/mnt/nvme0` stays empty.

**Expected behavior**

On a direct-I/O-capable filesystem like this one, stores should succeed with `use_odirect: true` — that's the whole point of running the cache on NVMe RAID0.

Failing that, LMCache should:
- include the underlying errno / `OSError` message in the `failed to store` log line, and
- probe `O_DIRECT` support on `base_path` **once at startup**, then either fail fast with an actionable message or fall back to buffered I/O — instead of raising per-chunk for the lifetime of the process.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.
```
[2026-08-02 14:09:16,887] LMCache ERROR: FSL2Adapter failed to store /mnt/nvme0/-SEP-data-medium-SEP-text-generation-models-SEP-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic-SEP-@0x01000100@1@2fd0d18a24695cedc65b54957836c1ddcde16bfbe2208c8c8425e4fec9c93441.data (fs_l2_adapter.py:629:lmcache.v1.distributed.l2_adapters.fs_l2_adapter)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/miphi/vllm_lib/lib/python3.10/site-packages/lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/fs_l2_adapter.py", line 611, in _execute_store
    await self._loop.run_in_executor(
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/home/miphi/vllm_lib/lib/python3.10/site-packages/lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/fs_l2_adapter.py", line 563, in _write_with_odirect
    os.write(fd, buf)
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
[2026-08-02 14:09:16,888] LMCache ERROR: Failed to O_DIRECT write /mnt/nvme0/-SEP-data-medium-SEP-text-generation-models-SEP-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic-SEP-@0x01000100@1@677b099d2ff7f7e2dfbc81af4814264cbe36de448429655a96659cca176790a0.tmp (fs_l2_adapter.py:565:lmcache.v1.distributed.l2_adapters.fs_l2_adapter)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/miphi/vllm_lib/lib/python3.10/site-packages/lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/fs_l2_adapter.py", line 563, in _write_with_odirect
    os.write(fd, buf)
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
```

**Environment**
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux x86_64), Python 3.10
 - LMCache version: 0.5.2
 - vLLM version: 0.24.0
 - GPU: 1× SM 8.6 (compute capability 8.6), no tensor parallelism

 - Storage: 4× NVMe in md RAID0 (`md0`, 512k chunks, 4000288768 blocks), mounted at `/mnt/nvme0`
 - Filesystem:
 ```
 Filesystem     Type  1K-blocks  Used  Available Use% Mounted on
/dev/md0       ext4 3936358896    28 3736328048   1% /mnt/nvme0
```

items.title: [Documentation Request] vLLM kv_load_failure_policy doesn't apply to load failures in L2 adapters
items.author: RedL0tus
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
Please label your issue so that it can easily be easily categorized under [LMCache Onboarding](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/1882)

**Summary**
[kv_load_failure_policy](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/api/vllm/config/kv_transfer/#vllm.config.kv_transfer.KVTransferConfig.kv_load_failure_policy) doesn't seem to apply to remote KV data load failures in L2 adapters.

**Details**
vLLM supports setting kv_load_failure_policy, which defines the behavior during KV load failures. However, this configuration option doesn't seem to apply to L2 adapters. We've tested the `nixl_store` L2 adapter and the `s3` L2 adapter with injected errors, and LMCache seems to treat L2 load failures as cache misses instead of failures.

is this an intentional design choice? It would be great to document the expected behavior of failures at different cache levels in LMCache.

**Steps / Reproduction (if applicable)**
1. Start LMCache with L2 adapter set to `nixl_store` with OBJ backend, or `s3`.
2. Start vLLM, use LMCache for KV cache offloading and internal prefix caching disabled with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.
3. Send data to vLLM and Intercept all GetObject calls to the S3 endpoint.

**Expected Outcome / Goal**
With `"kv_load_failure_policy": "fail"`, requests with external cache hits should return error code.

**Actual Outcome (if applicable)**
LMCache log errors to the console, vLLM proceed to serve all requests with recomputed KV data as if it's only a cache miss.

**Additional Context**
This issue was first discovered by [Anish Sana](mailto:anish.sana@hpe.com) under HPE's internal testing.

items.title: L1 eviction races async L2 store: chunks discarded before offload are never stored (persistent re-prefill under L1 pressure)
items.author: ShreyasBaasri07
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
Bug

**Describe the bug**
In LMCache v0.5.5 (MP mode), under L1 (CPU) memory pressure, freshly-computed KV chunks can be evicted from L1 before the asynchronous store controller offloads them to L2, so they are silently dropped and never written to L2 — even when L2 is large enough to hold the entire working set and has no eviction configured.

The result: with a shared-prefix (prefix-caching-style) workload, ~19% of requests permanently retrieve only the shared prefix (first half of the prompt) and re-prefill the unique tail on every recurrence, indefinitely. The half-hits persist through the whole run, not just warmup.

Root cause (confirmed in v0.5.5 source):

L1 eviction destination defaults to EvictionDestination.DISCARD — L1 eviction does not offload to L2 (lru.py, eviction_controller.py:193).
The StoreController offloads L1→L2 by reserve_read-ing keys received from an L1_WRITE_FINISHED notification. If a key was already discard-evicted in the meantime, reserve_read returns KEY_NOT_EXIST, the key is silently skipped from the store (only surfaced as an L1_READ_FAILED / lmcache_mp.l1_read_failure "not_found" anomaly), and it never reaches L2 (lmcache/v1/distributed/storage_controllers/store_controller.py:600-627).
So there is a race between L1 DISCARD eviction and the async L2 offload; the loser is silently never stored.

**To Reproduce**
Environment: LMCache v0.5.5, MP mode, L1 + L2 where L2 is sized to hold the full working set and has no L2 eviction, and L1 is smaller than the shared-prefix working set.

Start the LMCache MP server with a small L1 and one large L2 adapter (e.g. S3/filesystem), no L2 eviction:
lmcache server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6555 --chunk-size 256 \
  --l1-size-gb 60 --eviction-policy LRU \
  --l2-adapter '{"type":"s3", ... ,"max_capacity_gb":500}'

Start vLLM with LMCacheMPConnector (kv_role: kv_both), --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager.
Run a shared-prefix benchmark whose prefix pool exceeds L1. With aiperf/genai-perf
--prefix-prompt-length 4096 --num-prefix-prompts 150 \
--isl 4096 --osl 100 --num-dataset-entries 200 \
--concurrency 10 --random-seed 42 --benchmark-duration 1200

Here 150 prefixes × 4096 tokens ≈ 75 GB of prefix KV > 60 GB L1. Each request = 8192 tokens (4096 shared prefix + 4096 unique tail).

Grep the server log for Retrieved N tokens.

Observed — persistent prefix-only half-hits throughout the run (not just warmup)
Half-hits occur at ~20–32/min even in steady state, long after every one of the 200 fixed prompts has been served many times. Since retrieval is a contiguous match from token 0, Retrieved 4096 means "prefix found, tail missing → prefill." (Optionally, lmcache_mp.l1_read_failure / L1_READ_FAILED "not_found" events fire in the same window.)

Control: setting --num-prefix-prompts 10 (prefix pool now fits in L1) eliminates the half-hits — all requests become full 8192-token hits. So the trigger is specifically L1 < shared-prefix pool.

**Expected behavior**
Once a chunk is computed and admitted to L1, it should reliably be offloaded to L2 and remain retrievable regardless of L1 pressure. A chunk should not be silently dropped from the L2 store just because it was evicted from L1 before the async offload read it. Subsequent requests for the same prompt should be full L2 hits, not re-prefills, when L2 has capacity and no eviction.

**Screenshots**
N/A (server-side KV-cache behavior; log evidence included above).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
OS: Linux
LMCache: v0.5.5
vLLM: 0.26.0
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
Python: 3.12.3
GPU: NVIDIA L40S
Mode: MP (LMCacheMPConnector, kv_role: kv_both), --chunk-size 256, --l1-size-gb 60, L2 sized to hold full working set with no L2 eviction

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
N/A (not a mobile/browser issue)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

items.title: Restart-proof KV cache for llama-server: 40K-token TTFT 155s to 6s after reboot
items.author: qqkzlm
items.body_excerpt:
Every restart wipes your prefill. Server crash, box reboot, model reload — a 40K-token agentic prompt pays the full ~155s prefill again before the first token.

I patched llama-server to persist KV-cache prefix checkpoints to disk and auto-restore the longest matching prefix on boot. Same prompt after a restart: **first token in ~6s instead of ~155s** (2.1s disk read once + decode). No client changes, no re-architecture — the server just remembers.

Measured on GTX 1080 8GB, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, `-c 92160`:

- Cold: 151s prefill → first token at ~155s
- Warm (post-restart): 2.1s disk read (first request only) → first token at ~6s
- Checkpoints keyed by model + ctx + KV quant (wrong config = ignored, never corrupted); disk-budget eviction included

Single-commit patch (86KB): https://github.com/qqkzlm/llama-cpp-prompt-disk-cache — `git am` onto the PrismML `prism` branch, four flags (`--slot-save-path`, `--checkpoint-min-step`, `--ctx-checkpoints`, `--prompt-cache-disk-budget`).

One MoE lesson from the same box: keep experts on GPU, let KV follow the layers — pushing 20 MoE layers to CPU collapsed prefill 265→30 tok/s, which no cache can fix.

Happy to upstream behind a flag if maintainers are interested.

comments.author: qqkzlm
comments.body:
Update to the README since this went up — three things worth calling out for anyone trying it:

**1. Prebuilt CUDA binaries exist for both platforms.** The `v0.2.3` release ships `llama-server-win-cuda-v0.2.3.zip` and `llama-server-linux-cuda-v0.2.3.tar.gz`. The Linux package is built for `sm_61`/Pascal, so it also runs on GTX 10-series. No build needed:

```bash
./llama-server -m model.gguf -c 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --slot-save-path /var/tmp/kvstore/model \
  --prompt-cache-disk-budget 20 --checkpoint-min-step 2048 --ctx-checkpoints 64
```

**2. Only one flag is actually required.** `--slot-save-path` is the only one you must pass — `--prompt-cache-disk-budget` and `--prompt-cache-disk-path` are silently ignored without it, and entries land in `<slot-save-path>/pdcache`. `--prompt-cache-disk` is **enabled by default**, so passing it is optional; use `--no-prompt-cache-disk` to turn the cache off.

**3. Cache hits require a byte-identical prompt prefix.** Only the common prefix from token 0 onward is reused. If you prepend a timestamp or a random ID, everything after it misses and the cache is effectively unused. Put stable content first (system prompt, tool definitions, long docs) and per-turn content last — opencode / Claude Code already do this, so it works out of the box.

The README now has a "when does the cache hit / when does it miss" section covering this, a flag-duty table, and a Chinese-first three-step guide (the repo README is now Chinese-primary). A Windows `start-llama-server.bat` is included in the zip if you want a prompt-driven launcher instead of a command line.

Still happy to upstream this behind a flag if maintainers are interested — the whole feature is one commit touching `tools/server/server-prompt-disk.cpp` (~900 lines) plus slot/task integration.

items.title: [Bug] --strip-thinking-cache + retraction: release_kv_cache frees KV slots the radix tree still owns (double free)
items.author: sohom-cs
items.body_excerpt:
**Describe the bug**

With `--strip-thinking-cache`, `Req.owned_kv_len()` caps the owned length at the prompt once the request has reasoning tokens (#22373):

```python
if get_serving().strip_thinking_cache and self.reasoning_tokens > 0:
    return min(self.kv.kv_committed_len, len(self.origin_input_ids))
```

`release_kv_cache` then treats `[owned_kv_len, kv_allocated_len)` as over-allocated and frees it (`_release_overallocated_kv_indices`). That relies on nothing past the prompt being in the tree, i.e. on `cache_protected_len <= len(origin_input_ids)`.

A retracted request breaks that. It keeps `output_ids` and `reasoning_tokens` (`reset_for_retract` resets neither) and is re-prefilled over `prompt + output_ids`. After that prefill, `maybe_cache_unfinished_req` → `cache_unfinished_req` inserts the whole re-prefill, so `cache_protected_len = len(prompt) + len(earlier output)`. When the request finishes, or is retracted again:

- `cache_finished_req(owned_kv_len=P)` / `free_kv_row([(cache_protected_len, P)])` frees nothing, since `cache_protected_len > P`;
- `_release_overallocated_kv_indices(P, kv_allocated_len)` frees `[P, kv_allocated_len)`, and that includes `[P, cache_protected_len)`, which belongs to a tree node.

With `page_size > 1` and a prompt that doesn't end on a page boundary, the same thing happens through a different free: `cache_finished_req` frees its unaligned tail `[page_aligned(owned_kv_len), owned_kv_len)`, and that page is also tree-owned once `cache_protected_len > P` (e.g. page 4, P=10, `cache_protected_len`=12: the page holding positions 8–11 is freed while the tree keeps it).

Those slots are now both in the free list and referenced by the tree. When the node is evicted they are freed again. `available_size()` can exceed the pool size, and one `alloc()` can hand the same slot to two requests: silent KV corruption. The assert that would catch it (`start_p == end_p`) is skipped under `strip_thinking_cache`.

The PD decode resume path looks exposed in the same way (`process_prebuilt` caches the resumed request with `maybe_cache_unfinished_req`), but I have reproduced only the aggregated path.

**Reproduction** (CPU, main `0967a013c2a`, `UnifiedRadixCache`, 256-slot pool, prompt 8, 6 output tokens before the retraction, 3 decode steps after the re-prefill; real `cache_unfinished_req`, `release_kv_cache`, `evict`)

```
after re-prefill: cache_protected_len=14 (prompt=8)
owned_kv_len()=8 committed=17 allocated=17
[finish] available after release: +9 (expected +3)
[finish] slots freed while still referenced by the tree: [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
[finish] after evicting the tree: free list 262 entries, 256 unique; available_size 262 > pool 256
[finish] one alloc() of the whole pool hands out [9..14] twice
```

The same numbers with `is_insert=False` (a second retraction).

**Expected:** each KV slot is freed once.

**Proposed fix:** under `strip_thinking_cache`, never report less than `cache_protected_len`:

```python
return min(self.kv.kv_committed_len, max(len(self.origin_input_ids), self.kv.cache_protected_len))
```

The output the tree already holds (from the re-prefill) stays the tree's, and only the request-private tail is freed. Without a retraction, `cache_protected_len <= prompt`, so behaviour is unchanged.

I have this with a CPU test (finish, second retraction, the no-retraction case, and page_size=4 with aligned and unaligned prompts). I'm filing the issue first because two open PRs touch this code: #41281 (@hnyls2002) and #35694 (@alphabetc1), which changes `owned_kv_len`. The test still fails on the current heads of both (`1c912a5d6bb` and `5724c337c00`), and passes on both with the one-line change. In #41281's `insert_req` flow, `cache_protected_len` is lowered to the page-aligned `P` before the tail free, so the tree-owned slots are still freed. Happy to send it as a PR on top of whichever lands first, or for it to be folded into one of them.

items.title: [RFC][NPU] INT8 (C8) KV cache for DSA models (GLM-5.2) on Ascend A2/A3 (910B/910C)
items.author: qidaye
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

This RFC proposes generalizing the existing arch35-only packed FP8 DSA KV cache
to a "packed one-byte quant" path, so that GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) and
other DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA models can run an **INT8 (C8) KV cache on Ascend
A2/A3 (910B/910C)**. Every hardware question the proposal depends on has been
probed on a 910B (CANN 9.0.0, torch_npu 2.10.0); section 4 states measured
verdicts, not predictions.

Sections 1-4 of the full RFC follow. The remaining sections (change-surface
audit, test plan, confidence ledger) exist and can be posted here if useful;
a few forward references to them ("section 5" / "section 6" / "section 7")
remain in the text below -- the "section 7" material is summarized under
**Proposed contribution plan** at the end.

> All `file:line` references are against `sgl-project/sglang` at
> **`06008c170dae333e22caceb51f36224071f9b5b3`** (`[dsv4.1]Optimize FP4 indexer by
> skipping invisible tiles`, #40431), which is an ancestor of `upstream/main` --
> so every citation below is checkable against upstream as-is.
>
> vllm-ascend references are against **`abe8ff18a96bcd5f90d08077d1ccd068b959cab4`**
> and carry a `[va]` prefix, relative to that repo's root.
> ops-transformer references are against `gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer` at
> **`bcc6304656c9e712b50b1faa22872a158b1e34c5`** (the commit sgl-kernel-npu's CI
> pins; `bcc6304` below) and carry an `[ops-t]` prefix.

## 1. Motivation

SGLang today supports an 8-bit ("C8") KV cache for DSA models on Ascend **only on
arch35 / Ascend 950**, in the FP8-E4M3 packed form added by
`[NPU]Support GLM5.2 and FP8 DSA&Indexer kvcache for 950` (commit `3ff226ba8f`).
On A2/A3 the DSA KV cache is unconditionally BF16.

This matters because the KV cache is the binding constraint on A2-class hardware.
A representative single-node deployment (8x 910B, 64 GB/card, GLM-5.2-W4A8, TP8,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.85`):

| item | per card |
|---|---|
| weights | 49.67 GB |
| KV cache | 1.73 GB -> `max_total_num_tokens = 16768` |
| NPU graphs | 0.75 GB |
| unused | 8.25 GB |

`context_len` is 1 M, but the whole instance holds ~16 K tokens. Raising
`mem-fraction-static` helps, but the ceiling is still set by BF16 KV bytes/token.

Per token, per layer, for GLM-5.2 (`kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`,
`index_head_dim=128`):

| component | BF16 | INT8 packed | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| main MLA latent + rope | 1152 B | 656 B (512 int8 + 4x fp32 tile scales + 64x bf16 rope) | **1.76x** |
| indexer K | 256 B | 130 B (128 int8 + 1x fp16 scale) | **1.97x** |
| **total** | **1408 B** | **786 B** | **1.79x** |

The main-KV term dominates, so the expected end-to-end gain is ~1.6-1.8x more
resident tokens at the same memory budget. vllm-ascend reports a **measured
1.62x** for the equivalent change on GLM-5 W8A8 / A3 (75,600 -> 122,309 tokens,
PR #11228 / #11846) -- a second-hand figure from PR prose, but consistent with
the arithmetic above.

---

## 2. What exists today

### 2.1 The arch35 FP8 packed path (the template)

Storage is an **opaque fixed-width record**, one per token per layer, whose width is

```python
# python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py, calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim
kv_lora_rank + kv_lora_rank // quant_block_size * 4 + qk_rope_head_dim * rope_storage_dtype.itemsize
# GLM-5.2: 512 + 4*4 + 64*2 = 656 bytes
```

It is produced by `_pack_dsa_fp8_kv_cache`
(`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:839`):

```python
quantized, scale = torch_npu.npu_dynamic_quant(latent.reshape(-1, 128), dst_type=self.dtype)
packed = torch.cat((quantized.view(uint8),            # 512 B
                    cache_v.to(bf16).view(uint8),     # 128 B  rope, NOT quantized
                    scale.to(fp32).view(uint8)),      #  16 B  4 per-128-tile scales
                   dim=-1)
```

and consumed by `forward_sparse`
(`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py:1228`):

```python
torch_npu.npu_kv_quant_sparse_flash_attention(
    query=torch.cat((q_nope, q_pe), -1),   # bf16 [T, H, 576]
    key=packed, value=packed,
    key_quant_mode=2, value_quant_mode=2,
    key_dequant_scale=None, value_dequant_scale=None,   # scales read inline
    quant_scale_repo_mode=1, tile_size=128, rope_head_dim=64,
    layout_query="TND", layout_kv="PA_BSND", sparse_mode=3, attention_mode=2, ...)
```

**Key observation: the record layout is not FP8-specific.** It is "512 one-byte
values + per-128-tile FP32 scales + BF16 rope tail", and INT8 and FP8-E4M3 are
both one byte, so the 656-byte width, the `quant_scale_repo_mode=1` /
`tile_size=128` descriptor, and the `npu_dynamic_quant` call site
(`dst_type=self.dtype` already) carry over structurally. The quantization is
**dynamic** (per-token, per-128-tile, computed online), so no checkpoint
calibration is required.

The scale contract is settled, from two independent implementations: the
**main-KV** per-128-tile scale is **FP32 for INT8 and FP8 alike**, symmetric,
no zero-point (`[va] vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py:87-99` hardcodes an fp32
scale term in the record width regardless of KV dtype;
`[va] vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py:1991` has the INT8 branch cast the scale
`.to(torch.float32)`). The **indexer** per-token scale is a different buffer
entirely -- FP16 under INT8 on A2/A3, FP32 under FP8 on A5 -- and belongs to
section 2.2, not to this record.

Functional acceptance of this record with an INT8 payload on a 910B is now
**measured** (section 4, V1). Numerical parity against a BF16 reference remains
test item 1 in section 6.

items.title: Assertion in TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers: "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" on a pointer select inside a runtime scf.if
items.author: O1iveira7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling a legal Triton kernel fails with a C++ assertion in the AMD `TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` pass. The kernel merges two pointer bases with `tl.where` under a tensor condition inside a runtime `if`; the pass then hits a mixed representation between the two `scf.if` arms and aborts compilation.


**Error log**
```
CanonicalizePointers.cpp:1445: ... ConvertSCFIfOp::matchAndRewrite_(scf::IfOp, OneToNOpAdaptor, ...):
Assertion ifOp.thenYield()->hasAttr(kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets) &&
          "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" failed.
note: Pipeline failed while executing [TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` on 'tt.func' operation: @kernel]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

Failure is in `make_ttgir` (MLIR), before LLVM codegen; exit code 1.
```

The generated TTGIR is:

```
%5 = scf.if %4 -> (tensor<2x!tt.ptr<f32>>) {
  %11 = tt.addptr %10, %0          // base = splat(arg1)
  %12 = arith.select %9, %11, %2   // tensor condition, different bases
  scf.yield %12
} else {
  scf.yield %2                     // base = splat(arg2)
}
%8 = tt.load %5
```
TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers is a 1:N conversion to fat pointers (scalar base, tensor offset). scf.if is only rewritten after both scf.yields are rewritten (tracked via internal then/else-rewritten attributes). ConvertSCFYieldOp sets kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets on a yield only when one of its remapped operands is a 2-element fat pointer, while ConvertSCFIfOp unconditionally asserts that the then-yield has that attribute.

Here ConvertArithSelectOp takes its special case for a tensor condition with differing scalar bases and materializes both arms into full tensor pointers instead of a (base, offset) pair. So the then-yield carries a single materialized pointer and gets no fat-pointer index attribute, while the else-yield (a plain tt.addptr) converts to a fat pointer pair and does get the attribute. Both yields are marked rewritten, the scf.if becomes illegal, ConvertSCFIfOp fires, and the assertion fails on the inconsistent arms.

**Reproducer**
```
import os

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(sw, a_ptr, b_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    p = b_ptr + offs
    if tl.load(sw) == 0:
        p = tl.where(offs >= 0, a_ptr + offs, b_ptr + offs)
    tl.store(a_ptr + offs, tl.load(p))


def _main() -> None:
    device = "cuda"
    N = 2
    a = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    b = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    sw = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    print(f"REPRO_START N={N} buffer_ops={os.environ.get('AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS', 'default')}", flush=True)
    kernel[(1,)](sw, a, b, BLOCK=N, num_warps=1)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print("REPRO_DONE (no crash)", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()
```

### Environment details

- AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- triton-rocm 3.8.0, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2, Python 3.12.13

items.title: [RFC]: Qwen3-ASR pseudo-streaming can repeat or miss segments
items.author: shiverking
items.body_excerpt:
### Motivation.

I have been experimenting with Qwen3-ASR pseudo-streaming based on the `response_prefix` / prefix-feedback approach discussed in:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35908
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36018
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35894

Thanks to the contributors of these discussions and PRs. They provide a useful path for REST/realtime pseudo-streaming ASR.

In my local tests, this approach works well for English. After normalizing punctuation and whitespace, English content similarity between full-audio transcription and batched pseudo-streaming transcription can reach around `0.99`.

However, for Arabic/Thai and some Chinese cases, pseudo-streaming can enter repeated generation loops or miss transcript segments after repeated rounds are filtered. Based on these experiments, using `response_prefix` as the main mechanism for carrying streaming context does not seem robust enough for production multilingual ASR.

## Observations
The pseudo-streaming loop I tested is:

text
```
1. Split audio into chunks.
2. Send a sliding audio window to /v1/audio/transcriptions.
3. Keep stable transcript text locally.
4. Send stable text back as response_prefix.
5. Merge the new response into the final transcript.
```

For long audio, around 120 seconds, with 10-second chunks and a 30-second sliding window, I observed:

- English: content-normalized result is very close to full-audio transcription.
- Arabic/Thai: some windows can generate thousands of repeated words/tokens.
- Chinese: some windows can enter repeated short-phrase loops.
- Dropping repeated rounds avoids long repetition, but can miss valid transcript segments.
- Word-based prefix/holdback works better for English than for Chinese/Thai.
- Character-based prefix/holdback is more useful for Chinese/Thai.

Example repeated-generation pattern:
```
round=6 latency_ms=204617 ttft_ms=188 response_words=2993
round=7 latency_ms=200947 ttft_ms=132 response_words=2929
round=8 latency_ms=201293 ttft_ms=281 response_words=2929
```
This can reproduce with concurrency=1, so it does not appear to be a concurrency issue. Even if this loop is moved from the client side into a server-side realtime wrapper, the core mechanism is still accumulated/sliding audio plus text-prefix feedback, so the same accuracy risks remain.

I would like to propose adding true Engine-level streaming ASR support, where the engine keeps streaming session state across audio chunks instead of relying on caller-side or server-side pseudo-streaming with `response_prefix`.
This would address two separate issues:
- Accuracy: avoid changing decoding behavior through repeated independent window decoding and text-prefix feedback.
- Efficiency: avoid repeatedly uploading and/or re-encoding overlapping audio windows as the audio grows.

The key idea is Engine-level streaming， which is also mentioned in option B of 35908:

```text
one ASR streaming session
new audio chunks are appended to the same session
the engine preserves model context/cache across chunks
partial/final transcript is generated from the continuous session state
```

### Proposed Change.

I would like to discuss whether vLLM should treat `response_prefix`-based pseudo-streaming as a short-term workaround and move toward true Engine-level streaming ASR with preserved model/cache state.

Although client-side or server-side pseudo-streaming is easier to implement, my experiments suggest that it can introduce significant accuracy risks. Since each chunk/window is still decoded as a separate request and stitched together with prefix feedback, the result can diverge from full-context decoding. For some languages, this can lead to repeated generation, prefix pollution, or missing transcript segments after repetition filtering.

### Feedback Period.

No strict deadline. I am opening this to collect feedback from maintainers and contributors on the intended direction for streaming ASR support in vLLM.

### CC List.

cc @vllm-project/maintainers
Also cc contributors/reviewers from the related discussions if appropriate:
#35908
#36018
#35894

### Any Other Things.

Model: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B
API: /v1/audio/transcriptions
Streaming: SSE enabled
Audio length: around 120 seconds
Chunk size: 10 seconds
Sliding window: 30 seconds

items.title: [Bug]: Responses API streaming aborts mid-stream (nameless ResponseFunctionToolCallItem) with Qwen3.8 + qwen3_coder + DFlash speculative decoding
items.author: ruiwarn
items.body_excerpt:
### Current environment

- vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev1104` (main branch, 2026-08-22 dev build). Also verified that no released version up to and including v0.28.0 (2026-08-26) contains a fix for this bug.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B (FP8)
- Speculative decoding: DFlash drafter enabled
- `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`
- `--reasoning-parser qwen3`
- Client: `/v1/responses` with `stream: true` (via LiteLLM)

### 🐞 Describe the bug

In agentic (tool-heavy) workloads, the Responses API SSE stream aborts mid-stream with no terminal `response.*` event, leaving the client with an unclassifiable truncated stream. The failure is intermittent but recurrent.

### Error message

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ResponseFunctionToolCallItem
name
  Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]
...
RuntimeError: Caught handled exception, but response already started.
```

### Root cause analysis

The crash occurs when a single engine step spans the end of a tool call and the start of the following reasoning/content segment — speculative decoding makes such multi-boundary steps common.

`split_delta()` decomposes a compound `DeltaMessage` in the fixed order reasoning → content → tool_calls. When the tool-call part of the compound delta is the *argument tail* of an already-open tool call (its first `DeltaToolCall` carries no function name — e.g. the flush emitted by the parser engine at `</tool_call>`), replaying it *after* reasoning/content means the state machine has already transitioned away and closed the call. The tail then forces `SimpleStreamingEventProcessor.open()` to construct `ResponseFunctionToolCallItem(name=None)`, which fails pydantic validation. Because the SSE response has already started, the exception aborts the stream without any terminal event.

### Reproducing the problem

Serve the model with the configuration above, then send an agentic, tool-heavy prompt to `/v1/responses` with `stream: true`. The crash is intermittent (depends on where step boundaries fall relative to tool-call boundaries) but recurs reliably in tool-heavy workloads with speculative decoding enabled.

### Impact and workaround

We cannot use the `/v1/responses` streaming path for this deployment. As a workaround we set `use_chat_completions: true` in LiteLLM to route traffic through `/v1/chat/completions`, which loses the Responses API path for this deployment. There is no release containing a fix, so we are stuck on a dev build with no supported upgrade path.

items.title: [Bug]: CPU backend KV cache sizing error reports a negative size and recommends the wrong fix
items.author: mosafariuk
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` at `fc2c801ad9` (2026-09-30), CPU backend built from source
- macOS 27.0, Apple M1 (arm64), 8 GiB RAM, torch 2.13.0, Python 3.12
- The code path is platform-independent (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu_worker.py`)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the CPU worker's own footprint (model weights plus runtime) is larger than the memory reserved by `--gpu-memory-utilization`, startup fails with an error that contradicts itself and recommends the wrong fix:

```
ValueError: Available memory on node 0 (1.34/8.0 GiB) on kv cache allocation is less than requested memory for kv (-0.6/0.16 GiB). Reduce CPU memory used by other processes.
```

- It reports a **negative** KV request (`-0.6 GiB`) and calls 1.34 GiB "less than" it.
- The advice, "reduce CPU memory used by other processes", can't help: this worker has already used up its own reservation. What works is a larger `--gpu-memory-utilization`, or an explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` / `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`.
- On a machine with little free RAM, the startup check tells users to *decrease* `--gpu-memory-utilization`. Following that advice leads straight into this error, which then points somewhere else again.

Reproduction (default multiprocess engine):

```python
from vllm import LLM

if __name__ == "__main__":
    LLM(model="HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M", dtype="float32", max_model_len=512,
        enforce_eager=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.02)
```

With `gpu_memory_utilization=0.01` the error reads `(-0.46/0.08 GiB)`.

**Cause.** In `CPUWorker.determine_available_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu_worker.py:237-249`), `requested_memory_for_kv = requested_cpu_memory - rss`. The two failure conditions, `requested_memory_for_kv <= 0` (the worker outgrew its reservation) and `requested_memory_for_kv > available_memory` (the node is short of free memory), share one message. That message only fits the second case.

#42479 reworded the neighbouring CPU memory errors but did not touch this branch. Related: #29233.

items.title: [Feature]: Logprobs on parsed path streaming `/derender`
items.author: hickeyma
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Streaming `/derender` with a reasoning or tool parser (#50550) doesn't return logprobs. #55029 added streaming logprobs but only on the unparsed path. The parsed path builds its stream choices without them. A client that streams with `logprobs: true` through a parser gets nothing back.

Agreed on #47161 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161#issuecomment-5893681568): the engine is the reference for logprob token strings. Standalone `/derender`, including the parsed path should use one shared resolver built on `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` and `_correct_decoded_token` with parity tests against the engine.

Scope:

- Resolve each chunk's logprobs and attach them to whatever delta the parser emits. `/v1/chat/completions` does the same, with one `logprobs.content` list no matter which field the tokens land in.
- Update `logprob_context_token_ids` on the parsed path, like the plain path does. Keep it starting empty, like the engine.
- Drop logprobs on every chunk when `include_reasoning=false` with a parser, like the engine does.
- Fix batch derender too. `_derender_chat` clears `reasoning` but still returns the logprobs.
- Add parity tests against `/v1/chat/completions` with `include_reasoning` on and off, a chunk the parser swallows (tool-call markup) and a multi-byte char split across chunks.

`DerenderStreamState` stays as is. Chunk logprobs already cover only that chunk's tokens and replay never touches them, so no cursor is needed. #59510 handles streaming stop with a 400, so no pending text field either.

Blocked on #58181 (still open). The shared helper (`decode_token_ids`) and the parity tests depend on it.

@shimib has offered to take this. @hyeongyun0916 will review and help with repros.

### Alternatives

Re-resolving token strings separately in the parsed path. We ruled this out on #47161 because the paths already disagree (see #59241).

### Additional context

- #47161: RFC thread where this was agreed
- #55029: streaming logprobs for the unparsed path
- #50550: parser aware streaming derender
- #58181 / #57574: `GenerateLogProbs` with integer token IDs
- #59241 / #59252: SentencePiece leading space dropped in derender logprob strings
- #57052 / #59510: stop handling on derender. #59510 makes streaming `/derender` return 400 on `stop` and notes that logprobs aren't trimmed to the cut text.

[PP0] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 1023, ... #running-req: 1, ...
[PP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 6088, in run_scheduler_process
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1890, in run_event_loop
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5938, in dispatch_event_loop
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5947, in _dispatch_event_loop_once
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 165, in event_loop_pp
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 1727, in _pp_launch_batch
  File "sglang/srt/observability/scheduler_stage_metrics.py", line 155, in wrapper
  File "sglang/srt/utils/nvtx_utils.py", line 109, in wrapper
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4494, in run_batch
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 1392, in _pp_spec_rebuild_verify_input
AttributeError: 'EagleDraftInput' object has no attribute 'rids'
```

PP1 then dies with `gloo ... Connection closed by peer` and the server exits.

It looks like the mixed batch (`ForwardMode.MIXED`) is classified as a verify round in `run_batch` (`is_verify_round = pp_size > 1 and not (forward_mode.is_extend() or is_extend_in_batch)`, scheduler.py ~L4489), so `_pp_spec_rebuild_verify_input` expects a `PPSpecRelayInput` but gets the `EagleDraftInput` of the merged batch. The same code is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-10-05.

`speculative_hook.py` already disables mixed chunk for algorithms where `supports_mixed_chunk()` is false; EAGLE returns true there without considering `pp_size > 1`. Until the PP relay handles mixed batches, auto-disabling mixed chunk (with a warning) when `pp_size > 1` and spec is on would turn this crash into a config downgrade.

Without `--enable-mixed-chunk` the same setup works fine (PP=2 + MTP serving and benchmarks up to 255k-token prompts with 4 concurrent requests).

Note: requests that ask for `logprobs` are never mixed, so a benchmark that uses logprobs will not trigger this.

### Reproduction

Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (built-in MTP head), stock `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` image, no local patches. The memory-related flags are only there to fit 2x 16 GB GPUs.

```bash
SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1 SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=40,24 \
sglang serve \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8007 \
  --pp-size 2 \
  --json-model-override-args '{"language_model_only": true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --max-total-tokens 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.99 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --enable-linear-replayssm-spec \
  --enable-mixed-chunk
```

Client (one streaming request, then a ~4k-token prompt while it decodes):

```python
import json, threading, time, urllib.request
URL = "http://localhost:8007/v1/chat/completions"
def post(content, max_tokens, stream):
    body = {"model": "qwen3.8-27b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
            "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
        return sum(1 for _ in r) if stream else json.load(r)
t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: print("stream chunks:", post("Write a long story.", 1000, True)))
t.start(); time.sleep(3)
print("long prompt:", post("hello " * 4000 + "\nSummarize.", 16, False)["usage"])  # -> HTTP 500
t.join()
```

Result: the long prompt returns HTTP 500, the stream stops after a few chunks, and the server log shows the traceback above. Reproduces every time.

items.title: [Bug]: Realtime STT (Voxtral realtime): self-sustained blank-token rut mutes live transcription for minutes over real speech
items.author: damienlaine
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

A realtime transcription session (`/v1/realtime`, Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime, realtime STT path from #45833) can fall into a self-sustained decoding rut: the model emits the blank token (id 32) at every frame (12.5 tok/s) over real speech, for 1 to 20 minutes, then recovers on its own. The engine is perfectly healthy during the episode: steady 1 token/frame, no warnings, KV stable, WebSocket connected. The client just receives empty deltas while speech is flowing, and the audio of the hole is lost.

We reproduce it deterministically on a fixed audio file and have characterized the mechanism. A mitigation PR is linked below.

## Environment

- Realtime STT path as proposed in #45833 (observed on the linto-ai fork it comes from, at the commit matching the PR)
- Model: mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602, --tokenizer-mode mistral
- Observed on 3 GPUs (RTX A4000, L40S, RTX 4090 laptop), 3 different audio contents (2 audiobooks, 1 live radio stream), mono and multi-session, greedy and temperature 0.3, with and without long-session re-anchoring.

## Deterministic reproduction

Two concurrent realtime WebSocket sessions streaming the same public-domain French audiobook (LibriVox, "Le tour du monde en quatre-vingts jours", resampled 16 kHz mono) at 1x from offsets 2700 s and 5400 s, 30 ms paced appends.

Server:

```
vllm serve mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 --tokenizer-mode mistral \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --max-num-seqs 12 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"sliding_window":256},"audio_config":{"sliding_window":256}}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 --max-model-len 8192
```

The offset-5400 session goes mute at feed time 1183 s (mid-sentence), stays mute for 179 s (2236 consecutive blank frames), and recovers by itself. Reproduced 8/8, onset stable to 0.1 s, recovery token identical across runs. Trap positions are content-specific: a different long recording will have its own, at other positions.

Harness (self-contained, websockets + soundfile + numpy):

<details>
<summary>collapse_probe.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Silent-collapse repro bench for the local 4090 (direct WS, no transcriber).

Streams N desynced channels of the audiobook into the realtime server, with
staggered admissions (the most frequent trigger seen on the L40S run). Each
channel logs non-empty deltas and raises a GAP alarm when no non-empty delta
arrived for GAP_S seconds while audio keeps being fed. Empty deltas received
during the gap are counted: empties flowing = session alive = rut signature
(as opposed to a dead/disconnected session).

Usage: collapse_probe.py [initial_channels] [max_channels] [admit_every_s]
Stop with Ctrl-C / SIGTERM: prints a final gap report.
"""
import asyncio, base64, json, os, signal, sys, time
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf, websockets

URI = os.environ.get("PROBE_URI", "ws://localhost:8000/v1/realtime")
MODEL = "mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602"
AUDIO = os.environ.get("PROBE_AUDIO", "audiobook_16k_mono.wav")
SR = 16000
FRAME_MS = 30
GAP_S = 60          # no non-empty delta for this long => gap
STATUS_EVERY_S = 60
CHANNEL_OFFSET_S = float(os.environ.get("PROBE_CHANNEL_OFFSET_S", "2700"))  # spacing between channel start positions
# Added to every channel's start position (solo replay of a known rut trigger)
BASE_OFFSET_S = float(os.environ.get("PROBE_BASE_OFFSET_S", "0"))
# If set, append every non-empty delta to <dir>/chNN_transcript.txt (for WER)
DUMP_DIR = os.environ.get("PROBE_DUMP_DIR", "")

N_INIT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 4
N_MAX = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 10
ADMIT_EVERY_S = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 600.0

T0 = time.time()
def log(msg):
    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}][+{time.time()-T0:8.1f}s] {msg}", flush=True)

GAPS = []  # closed gaps: dicts(ch, onset_wall, dur_s, empties, fed_s_at_onset)

class Channel:
    def __init__(self, idx):
        self.idx = idx
        self.tag = f"ch{idx:02d}"
        self.fed_s = 0.0
        self.words = 0
        self.deltas_any = 0
        self.deltas_empty = 0
        self.last_nonempty = None   # wall time of last non-empty delta
        self.last_any = None
        self.gap_open = None        # dict while a gap is open
        self.connected = False
        self.tail = ""
        self.dump_fh = open(f"{DUMP_DIR}/{self.tag}_transcript.txt", "a",
                            buffering=1) if DUMP_DIR else None

    async def run(self):
        f = sf.SoundFile(AUDIO)
        f.seek(int((BASE_OFFSET_S + self.idx * CHANNEL_OFFSET_S) * SR) % max(1, len(f) - SR))
        frame = int(FRAME_MS / 1000 * SR)
        try:
            async with websockets.connect(URI, max_size=None, ping_interval=20) as ws:
                hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
                log(f"{self.tag} ADMITTED id={hello.get('id')} book_offset={BASE_OFFSET_S + self.idx*CHANNEL_OFFSET_S:.0f}s")
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "session.update", "model": MODEL}))
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"}))
                self.connected = True
                start = time.time()
                recv_task = asyncio.create_task(self.receiver(ws))
                next_t = time.time()
                while True:
                    data = f.read(frame, dtype="float32")
                    if data.ndim > 1: data = data[:, 0]
                    if len(data) == 0:
                        f.seek(0); continue
                    pcm = (data * 32767).astype(np.int16).tobytes()
                    await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "input_audio_buffer.append",
                                              "audio": base64.b64encode(pcm).decode()}))
                    self.fed_s += len(data) / SR
                    self.check_gap()
                    next_t += FRAME_MS / 1000
                    slack = next_t - time.time()
                    if slack > 0: await asyncio.sl
