items.title: [Store] remove + re-put of the same key never re-offloads with the bucket backend
items.author: he-yufeng
items.body_excerpt:
While extending the regression coverage on #3889 I hit an offload quirk that looks worth its own report.

Repro, in-proc master harness with `bucket_storage_backend` and `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT=1`:

1. `put(key)` then the object offloads, LOCAL_DISK replica R1 registered.
2. `remove(key)`, master record erased.
3. `put(key)` again, fresh memory replica, PutEnd queues the offload task.
4. The next heartbeat takes the task but the key comes back as a NACK (`data_size=-1`) and no new disk replica ever registers. The object stays memory-only indefinitely.

What happens on the client: `FileStorage::OffloadObjects` finds the local slices fine, but `BucketStorageBackend` still holds the key in `object_bucket_map_` from the first offload (remove never reaches the backend), so `BatchOffload` skips it as an already-persisted duplicate without invoking the completion callback, and `FileStorage` NACKs it per the "a successful batch may skip duplicates" contract. The master erases the offload marker on the NACK, so the key can never be offloaded again until the backend evicts the stale entry.

Two consequences:

- Durability: a re-put object silently loses its disk tier. If the memory replica is later evicted the object is gone, even with free SSD capacity.
- Staleness: the backend map still points at the old bucket file with the old bytes. Nothing serves it while the master holds no disk record, but a rescan-based path (master restart + `ReRegisterOffloadedObjects`) looks like it could re-register the old bytes under the new object. I have not verified that second path end to end.

Possible directions: propagate `remove()` to the storage backend so the persisted entry drops with the master record, or let `BatchOffload` overwrite a persisted entry under a generation check instead of skipping it.

Observed on current main (ubuntu 22.04 container, gcc) while testing #3889. I have the full glog trace (heartbeat takes the task, backend processes zero keys, NACK goes back, master cleans the marker) if useful.

items.title: Refactor: TRTLLMHAAttnBackend should not inherit from FlashInferAttnBackend when reuse is small
items.author: merrymercy
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

`TRTLLMHAAttnBackend(FlashInferAttnBackend)` (in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`) inherits from `FlashInferAttnBackend`, but it reuses very little from the parent. Almost all attention-specific behavior is overridden, and some inherited setup is allocated-but-never-used. We should reconsider this inheritance: **if the reuse is small, we should not inherit from `FlashInferAttnBackend`** — inheriting directly from the base `AttentionBackend` (and pulling in only the small bits of plumbing that are actually shared) would be cleaner.

### What is actually reused

The only real reuse comes from `super().__init__(...)`:
- `req_to_token_pool`, `token_to_kv_pool`
- `max_context_len`, `skip_prefill`, `use_sliding_window_kv_pool`
- the `kv_indptr` / `kv_last_page_len` buffers (used by the companion `TRTLLMHAAttnMultiStepDraftBackend` draft steps)
- `forward()` dispatch — which actually comes from the base `AttentionBackend`, not from FlashInfer.

### What is overridden (not reused)

Essentially all the attention logic:
- `init_forward_metadata`, `init_cuda_graph_state`, `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`
- `forward_decode`, `forward_extend` (call `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` / `flashinfer.prefill.trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` directly)
- `get_cuda_graph_seq_len_fill_value`, `_resolve_swa_kv_pool`
- it uses its own `TRTLLMMHAMetadata` and its own page-table builder.

### Inherited-but-unused / redundant work

Because the TRTLLM kernels use a completely different API, part of the parent `__init__` is wasted:
- Parent builds `prefill_wrapper_ragged`, `prefill_wrappers_paged`, `decode_wrappers`, and the `FlashInferIndicesUpdater*` objects — TRTLLM-MHA never uses them.
- Parent sets `self.workspace_buffer` to the shared `global_workspace_buffer`, but the child **replaces** it with its own zero-init `global_zero_init_workspace_buffer`.
- `max_context_len` and `_swa_kv_pool` are set by the parent and then re-set by the child.

### Proposal

- Evaluate inheriting `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` directly from `AttentionBackend` instead of `FlashInferAttnBackend`.
- Move the small amount of genuinely shared init plumbing into a thin shared helper/mixin (e.g. pool/buffer setup) rather than dragging in the full FlashInfer wrapper/indices-updater allocation.
- Avoid allocating FlashInfer wrappers and updaters that the TRTLLM path never uses.
- Apply the same review to `TRTLLMHAAttnMultiStepDraftBackend(FlashInferMultiStepDraftBackend)`.

As a general guideline: **do not inherit from `FlashInferAttnBackend` when the reuse is little** — prefer inheriting from the base `AttentionBackend` and sharing only what is actually common.

### Good first issue

This is a good first issue: it is well-scoped, localized to `trtllm_mha_backend.py` (plus the base classes), and mostly a refactor with clear before/after behavior to validate against existing tests.

items.title: [Bug] Glm4MoeDetector: a string parameter whose value is valid JSON is rewritten (a quoted literal loses its quotes, true becomes True)
items.author: krisztian-gajdar
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`Glm4MoeDetector` (the `glm` / `glm45` tool-call parser for GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.6) changes the value of a string parameter in non-streaming parsing. `parse_arguments` first tries `json.loads(json_value)` ([glm4_moe_detector.py#L102](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/209e190ee568d346abb50b5d4bd0cb0d2192a73d/python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py#L102)), and `_parse_argument_pairs` turns the result back into a string for a string parameter ([L644-L652](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/209e190ee568d346abb50b5d4bd0cb0d2192a73d/python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py#L644-L652)). So a value that happens to be valid JSON is rewritten:

- `"hello"` (with quotes) becomes `hello`
- `true` becomes `True`
- `null` becomes `None`
- `1e2` becomes `100.0`
- `{"k":1}` becomes `{"k": 1}`

The GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.6 chat templates write a string value raw (`<arg_value>{{ v | tojson(ensure_ascii=False) if v is not string else v }}</arg_value>` in [zai-org/GLM-4.5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.5/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) and [zai-org/GLM-4.6](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6/blob/main/chat_template.jinja)), so for a parameter declared as a string the raw text is the value.

The streaming path of the same detector already keeps the raw text, so streaming and non-streaming return different arguments for the same output. `prev_tool_call_arr`, which `_parse_argument_pairs` fills when a streamed call finishes, disagrees with the streamed arguments too.

This is the GLM-4.5/4.6 counterpart of #42765 (`Glm47MoeDetector`). `Ling3Detector` inherits `_parse_argument_pairs` from `Glm4MoeDetector`, and the [Ling-3.0-flash chat template](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) also writes string values raw.

### Reproduction

At `209e190ee568d346abb50b5d4bd0cb0d2192a73d`:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.glm4_moe_detector import Glm4MoeDetector

tools = [
    Tool(
        type="function",
        function={
            "name": "edit_file",
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"new_str": {"type": "string"}}},
        },
    )
]
for value in ['"hello"', "true", "null", "1e2"]:
    text = f"<tool_call>edit_file\n<arg_key>new_str</arg_key>\n<arg_value>{value}</arg_value>\n</tool_call>"
    print([call.parameters for call in Glm4MoeDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls])
# ['{"new_str": "hello"}']
# ['{"new_str": "True"}']
# ['{"new_str": "None"}']
# ['{"new_str": "100.0"}']
```

Feeding the same text to `parse_streaming_increment` gives `{"new_str": "\"hello\""}`, `{"new_str": "true"}`, `{"new_str": "null"}` and `{"new_str": "1e2"}`.

### Expected

`{"new_str": "\"hello\""}`, `{"new_str": "true"}`, `{"new_str": "null"}` and `{"new_str": "1e2"}` from both paths. For a parameter declared as a string, the template wrote the value raw, so the raw text is the value.

items.title: Multimodal content-part uuid has no length bound and reaches the EngineCore block-hash pickle+SHA-256 path (uncapped sibling of the cache_salt fix)
items.author: AUTHENSOR
items.body_excerpt:
# Multimodal content-part `uuid` has no length bound and reaches the EngineCore block-hash pickle+SHA-256 path (uncapped sibling of the cache_salt fix)

**Severity: medium** (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption; same class and sink as GHSA-wpww-v874-ph2p)

**Affected:** vLLM main at commit `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3` (post-0.29.0); the `uuid` content-part field predates this commit.

## Summary

GHSA-wpww-v874-ph2p fixed scheduler-thread CPU exhaustion through oversized `cache_salt` by adding `validate_cache_salt` (128-char cap plus forbidden characters) and wiring it into the chat, completion, responses, pooling and scale-out protocols. The multimodal content-part `uuid` field flows into the exact same pickle+SHA-256 block-hash sink on the EngineCore scheduler thread, and nothing on its path bounds its length. An unauthenticated client of a multimodal endpoint can send a multi-megabyte `uuid` on one image part and cost the shared scheduler thread an O(uuid bytes) serialization per request, stalling unrelated tenants, identical to the capped attack.

## Mechanism (pin `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`)

1. The content part is parsed with no bound and only a str coercion: `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:1916-1918`, `uuid = part.get("uuid", None)` / `if uuid is not None: uuid = str(uuid)`.
2. The tracker materializes it into `mm_uuids` (`vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:825-875`), and `parse_mm_uuids` is a shape-only normalizer with no validation (`vllm/multimodal/parse.py:847-854`).
3. When the request carries no media_io/hf-processor kwargs (the default), the client string is used verbatim as the item hash (`vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:89-104`, "If there are no extra kwargs, use the client-provided UUID"); with kwargs present the same string is serialized into `MultiModalHasher.hash_kwargs` instead.
4. That hash becomes the feature identifier (`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:406-420`), which is carried into the EngineCore request.
5. `Request.__init__` runs `update_block_hashes()` on the engine core (`vllm/v1/request.py:224`), and the identifier is placed into block-0 extra keys (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:601-633`).
6. `hash_block_tokens` hashes the whole tuple with `sha256(pickle.dumps(...))` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:638-660`, `vllm/utils/hashing.py:26-30`), O(uuid bytes) of serialization on the single scheduler thread.

The security documentation covers uuid collision risk in multi-tenant deployments but sets no length expectation and no bound is enforced anywhere on the path.

## Reproduction (real decision functions at the pin)

A harness executes the verbatim functions extracted at the pinned commit:

- Control: `validate_cache_salt("A" * 129)` is rejected; 128 chars accepted (the shipped fix).
- Sibling gate: `parse_mm_uuids({"image": [<64 MiB string>]})` accepts it and returns the identical object.
- Sink: `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` + `hash_block_tokens` with a 64 MiB identifier produce a block-0 hash whose pickle payload is 67,108,955 bytes, measured at 0.1-1s per request versus under 10 ms for a normal 43-char uuid (the same sink caps `cache_salt` at 128 chars, payload 203 bytes).

Byte amplification over a normal uuid is 550,073x. Scaling matches the published GHSA measurements for equally sized salts (10 MB about 58 ms, 200 MB about 1.2 s end to end). Outputs are byte-identical across double runs.

## Impact

Unauthenticated remote CPU exhaustion of the shared EngineCore scheduler thread on any multimodal chat, responses or pooling deployment; concurrent oversized-uuid requests stall all tenants' requests. Same availability impact and prerequisites as GHSA-wpww-v874-ph2p (no auth by default, no feature flag, no body-size limit by default).

## Recommended fix

Bound the uuid at the parse boundary with the same policy applied to `cache_salt`: reject `uuid` values longer than a small constant (128 characters is ample for a UUIDv4 or base64 256-bit value) at the content-part parse in `chat_utils.py` or in `parse_mm_uuids`, mirroring `validate_cache_salt`, and document the limit beside the existing multi-tenant uuid guidance.

items.title: [Bug]: `LLM.generate()` never returns when `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0`
items.author: the-Shallow
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.28.0 on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `SchedulerConfig.max_num_scheduled_tokens` uses a lower bound of `ge=0`, so vLLM accepts zero as a valid scheduling budget. The engine then has no tokens available to schedule: initialization succeeds, but `generate()` makes no progress and never returns or reports an error. ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", max_num_scheduled_tokens=0, ) print(llm.generate( ["Hello, my name is"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=8), )) ``` ### Expected behavior vLLM should reject `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0` during configuration with a clear `ValueError`. An accepted configuration should not cause an unbounded silent hang. ### Suggested fix Require `max_num_scheduled_tokens` to be greater than zero and apply the existing non-positive-budget validation regardless of whether speculative decoding is enabled. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: MP mode: remaining unbounded request-state retention in vLLM client and sidecar prefetch bookkeeping
items.author: wuwanxu
items.body_excerpt:
## Deployment

We run a production **3P1D** deployment with vLLM and `LMCacheMPConnector`. Each serving node has a per-node LMCache sidecar; LMCache uses `fs_native` as the L2 adapter backed by local SSD. P2P, CacheBlend, and engine-driven transfer are not enabled.

The previous client-side MQ no-response leak is tracked separately in #5270. During a follow-up audit of upstream `dev` (checked at `05fc77a`, 2026-09-24), we found the two request-state retention paths below. This issue only reports the observed behavior and asks maintainers to determine the intended lifecycle and remediation.

## 1. vLLM client: `_returned_finished` grows for the worker lifetime

`LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter` creates:

```python
self._returned_finished: set[str] = set()
```

`_process_finished_stores()` uses this set to prevent a request ID from being reported repeatedly through `finished_sending`, then records returned IDs with:

```python
self._returned_finished.update(ret_stores)
```

We could not find a `discard`, `clear`, TTL, or capacity-based removal path. Therefore every request ID once returned as `finished_sending` remains resident until the vLLM worker exits. This path is exercised by normal successful requests as well as failure paths.

The set appears to be needed for async-scheduling deduplication after neighboring tracking sets are drained, but it also produces monotonic process-lifetime growth. With UUID-like Python request IDs, the retained footprint is roughly 150-200 bytes per request before allocator overhead; at sustained high QPS this can become material in a long-lived worker.

Relevant code:
- `lmcache/integration/vllm/vllm_multi_process_adapter.py` (`_returned_finished`, `_process_finished_stores`)

### Questions for maintainers

1. Is process-lifetime retention of every completed `finished_sending` request ID required by the vLLM connector contract?
2. What lifecycle or retention semantics should this deduplication state have in a long-running worker?

## 2. sidecar: abandoned prefetch jobs and completion Bitmaps are never reclaimed

`LookupModule` registers every lookup in:

```python
self._prefetch_jobs: dict[str, _PrefetchJob] = {}
```

The job is removed when `QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS` or `WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS` obtains a non-`None` completion result. If a client aborts or disconnects after LOOKUP, or stops polling after an RPC timeout/unhealthy transition, the job is not consumed by that path.

The corresponding `PrefetchController` completion state has the same consumer-driven ownership:

```python
self._completed_lookups: dict[PrefetchRequestId, int] = {}
self._completed_results: dict[PrefetchRequestId, Bitmap] = {}
```

`query_prefetch_result()` pops both the Bitmap and the lookup result. The source comment notes that failing to consume the prefetch result leaks memory. `Bitmap` is native/C++ memory, so its growth may not be visible in Python GC or tracemalloc. `END_SESSION` removes the session and touches L1 keys but does not remove the prefetch job or controller completion state.

In production we also see frequent `Session ... not found, skipping touch` warnings (roughly 378-953 over two hours), consistent with request-lifecycle skew and making normal client polling an unreliable sole ownership mechanism.

Relevant code:
- `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/lookup.py` (`_prefetch_jobs`, `query_prefetch_status`, `end_session`)
- `lmcache/v1/distributed/storage_controllers/prefetch_controller.py` (`_completed_lookups`, `_completed_results`, `query_prefetch_result`)

### Questions for maintainers

1. What is the intended owner of a prefetch job and its completion result after the original client has abandoned the request?
2. Is there an existing cancellation or reclamation lifecycle that this MP path should use?
3. What cleanup ordering is required for an in-flight prefetch so that late completion cannot expose invalid L1 data or retain completion state?

## Expected behavior

For healthy-sidecar and abort/error paths alike, client and server request bookkeeping should have a defined bounded lifecycle. Abandoned request state should be reclaimable without requiring a vLLM worker or sidecar restart, while preserving correctness for normal in-flight requests.

## Reproduction direction

1. Run vLLM + `LMCacheMPConnector` + sidecar with an SSD-backed `fs_native` L2.
2. Send sustained requests and observe the vLLM worker: `_returned_finished` grows monotonically.
3. Submit LOOKUPs, then abort/disconnect before prefetch polling completes, or induce a prefetch-status timeout.
4. Observe `lmcache_mp.active_prefetch_jobs` and `PrefetchController.report_status()["completed_results_count"]`; entries can remain after the client has abandoned the request.

comments.author: neevmodh
comments.body:
Read through both paths in `upstream/dev` to check the analysis — can confirm both observations.

**Part 1 (`_returned_finished`):** Confirmed there's no eviction path on this set anywhere in `vllm_multi_process_adapter.py`. Looking at `_process_finished_stores`, the set's only real job is to stop the same `req_id` from being re-added to `ret_stores` if `finished_req_ids_from_engine` reports it again in a later call — but once vLLM's own engine stops mentioning a `req_id` (i.e. it's fully retired from the engine's tracking), `_returned_finished`'s entry for it can never be hit again by the loop that checks it, so it's dead weight from that point on. A conservative fix that doesn't touch the dedup semantics: at the end of `_process_finished_stores`, intersect `_returned_finished` with the union of `self.finished_stores` / `self.store_futures` / `finished_req_ids_from_engine`, so an ID is only retained while it's still reachable through one of the sets that could re-report it. Happy to send that as a small PR if a maintainer confirms there's no other call site relying on longer retention.

**Part 2 (prefetch jobs):** Confirmed `end_session` (`lookup.py:514`) is already the natural per-request teardown hook — it's called on `MP_REQUEST_END` and already knows the `request_id`. Adding `self._prefetch_jobs.pop(request_id, None)` there looks safe on the `LookupModule` side. The harder part is `PrefetchController`'s `_completed_lookups`/`_completed_results` (a *different* class, presumably reachable through session/controller wiring I didn't fully trace) — and your question #3 is the real blocker here: popping a `Bitmap` out from under a prefetch that completes *after* the client has already been torn down risks exactly the late-completion/invalid-L1-data race you flagged, since it's native memory. I don't think this half should be fixed without a maintainer confirming the intended ownership handoff at session end — happy to implement once that's settled, but I'd rather not guess at a fix that touches native memory lifecycle across processes.

comments.author: neevmodh
comments.body: Following up on my earlier analysis: opened #5363 for part 1 (the `_returned_finished` set). Rather than guess at exact removal timing (which depends on the vLLM engine-contract question I couldn't answer myself), it bounds the set with a small LRU cap instead — converts unbounded growth into bounded memory without needing that question resolved first. Part 2 (sidecar prefetch/completion state) is intentionally left alone, per my earlier comment on the native-memory ordering risk.

## Checklist

* [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
* [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Motivation

`PoolName`, `PoolTransfer`, `PoolHitPolicy`, and `PoolTransferResult` are currently defined in `hicache_storage.py`.

These types are no longer really HiCache-specific. They are also used by Unified Cache, `pool_host`, NIXL, HF3FS, and other cache/storage code.

This makes imports like this a bit confusing:

```python
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import PoolName, PoolTransfer
```

Code that has nothing to do with HiCache still has to depend on a module named `hicache_storage`.

Would it make sense to move these shared types into a neutral module, for example:

```text
mem_cache/pool_transfer.py
```

and let `hicache_storage.py` import/re-export them for compatibility?

This should only be a code organization change, with no behavior change.

Current users include:

* `unified_cache/unified_cache_linker.py`
* `unified_cache/components/full_component.py`
* `pool_host/group.py`

items.title: [Bug]: Default -O2 leaves DeepSeek MLA RoPE and KV-cache fusion off
items.author: Aravind-11
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

This is a config-default bug read from source on `vllm-project/vllm` main `d77cf8115601f2856aacbfdd82a436ee78a558e6` (2026-10-07). The same gating is on `b6d8e8afd985f5711eee68e343d2ce908d166488`.

`python collect_env.py` was not run. The pinned torch is 2.13.0. The machine used for the reading has torch 2.5.1, which cannot import current main (`torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass`, `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`). No GPU run was done.

### Describe the bug

At default `-O2`, DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA never takes the existing RoPE + KV-cache fusion.

`MLARoPEKVCacheCatFusionPass` matches `k_pe.unsqueeze`, DeepSeek YaRN (or plain RoPE) on that slice, and `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update`, then replaces them with `fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update` (`ops.concat_and_cache_mla_rope_fused`). The pass is added only when `pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` is true (`vllm/compilation/passes/pass_manager.py`).

`-O2` sets that flag from `enable_rope_kvcache_mla_fusion`. The function is true only when `use_inductor_graph_partition` is on, or when `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` is false. The default is partition off, `splitting_ops is None`, and `fuse_attn_quant` is false (`IS_QUANTIZED` is hard-coded false), so the predicate returns true early: both cache-update ops will be appended. The flag therefore stays false.

`set_splitting_ops_for_v1` then appends `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` because of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33267. Dynamo splits the graph on that op, so the fusion pattern is not in one compiled piece.

Forcing `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla=True` without `use_inductor_graph_partition=True` does not warn. `fuse_rope_kvcache` and `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` are disabled in that situation. The MLA flag stays true, the pass is registered, and it matches nothing. The benchmark command on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45573 is that shape: the flag is set, `use_inductor_graph_partition` is not.

On the pinned torch (2.13), `_USE_LAYERNAME` is true unless `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0`. `LayerName` is a hoisted value-type opaque object, so torch.compile lifts the layer name as a graph input instead of a per-layer string constant. The #33267 reason for splitting this op out does not apply on a normal install. The non-MLA op `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` should stay split, because the AITER RoPE+KV fusions are a different path.

What this is not:

- DeepSeek-V4 does not reach this pass. `DeepseekV4Attention` is not an `MLAAttention`, and the CUDA Q/K path is `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_*_insert`, not `rotary_emb` plus `unified_mla_kv_cache_update`.
- This does not replace the manual-fusion rewrite in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43504 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45573.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50758 is the fallback for when `LayerName` is off. It is not this bug.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40392 added the pass. Its serve command sets both the flag and `use_inductor_graph_partition=True`, which is why that path works.

### Proposed fix

Keep the existing pass. At `-O2`, turn `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` on for CUDA/ROCm MLA models when `_USE_LAYERNAME` is set and `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` is not already a splitting op. In `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`, do not append that op in that case, so the pattern is in one Dynamo piece. Still append `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update`.

Leave the flag off when:

- the model is not MLA, or there is no model config (bare `VllmConfig()` splitting-ops snapshots stay as they are)
- the platform is not CUDA or ROCm
- `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0` or torch is older than 2.11
- HiSparse is on and Inductor graph partition is off (`prepare_kv_cache_update` has to run every step; HiSparseConnector can turn HiSparse on after the `-O2` default is applied)

If the flag is true and the op is still a splitting op with partition off, warn and set the flag false, same as the other RoPE+KV fusions.

Do not turn `use_inductor_graph_partition` on by default. Do not change `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update`, or the AITER `fuse_rope_kvcache` default flips on and is then forced off.

`-O0` and `-O1` keep the flag false.

I searched open issues for `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` and `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` and did not find a report of this default. I did not use the documentation chatbot.

- [x] Searched existing issues, including #33267, #43504, #45573, #50758, and #40392.

items.title: OTel tracing overhead cliffs at c=50 on TP=2 deployments — level/flush tuning has no effect
items.author: wangxf1987
items.body_excerpt:
## Title

OTel trace overhead benchmark on a production-style K8s deployment (TP=2, 2 replicas): throughput loss of 20-33% at c>=50, trace level and flush threshold have negligible effect

## Summary

We benchmarked `--enable-trace` overhead on a production-shaped K8s deployment (RBG + LeaderWorkerSet, not docker-compose), Qwen3.6-27B-CHO on sglang v0.5.18, TP=2 per replica x 2 replicas (4 GPUs total, not an exclusive full node). This complements the larger-scale results already discussed elsewhere for TP=8 exclusive-node setups, and shows the overhead shape is very different at smaller TP.

Full report (charts + tables): attached PDF (`report-en.pdf`). Raw data (`result.csv`, GPU/CPU logs) available on request.

## Environment

- sglang `v0.5.18` (community image), `SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC=1`
- Deployment: K8s RBG + LeaderWorkerSet, TP=2 per replica, 2 replicas, 4x H20 GPUs
- Trace path: sglang engine -> local OTel Agent (DaemonSet, node-local endpoint) -> Gateway -> backend, i.e. a two-hop agent-gw architecture, not a direct hardcoded Gateway connection
- 4 configs compared:
  | Group | trace level | async | flush threshold |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | G1 baseline | disabled | - | - |
  | G2 | 2 | 1 | default |
  | G3 | 3 | 1 | default |
  | G4 | 2 | 1 | 50 |
- Load generator: fixed-prompt benchmark client, concurrency swept across 1/10/50/100/200, 3 repeats per level (median)

## Findings

1. **Overhead is mild at low concurrency (c<=10)**: ttft_p99 +6~71%, throughput loss only 3~4%.
2. **c=50 is a clear inflection point**: ttft_p99 jumps 4.6x (172ms -> 965ms) going from G1 to G2 — roughly equivalent to the G1 baseline's own c=100 latency level being pulled forward to c=50. In other words, enabling trace shifts the whole latency-saturation curve left by one concurrency tier.
3. **From c>=50 onward, throughput loss is stable at 20~33%**, and grows with concurrency (-20.3% at c=50, up to -33.1% at c=200).
4. **Trace level 2 -> 3 produced no measurable incremental overhead** at c>=10 (all deltas within noise, ±2%).
5. **`SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC_FLUSH_THRESHOLD=50` vs. default also produced no measurable benefit** at c>=50 (within ±16%, mostly ±2%; one anomalous +132.9% ttft_p99 spike at c=10 looked like a transient one-off, not reproduced at other levels).
6. **Root cause for (4) and (5): CPU was never the bottleneck in this setup.** Host CPU utilization on the GPU node stayed at 2~3% across all 4 groups (vs. GPU sm% rising from 14.8% baseline to 16~19% with trace enabled). Both trace-level and flush-threshold tuning target CPU-side span processing cost — with only 2 TP ranks, span volume is low enough that CPU headroom is never exhausted, so those knobs have nothing to bite on at this scale.
7. This is a **much smaller overhead** than what we see at TP=8 on an exclusive full node (throughput loss there was 75~79%, itl_p99 spiking ~28x, with CPU pegged at 99% — happy to share that data too if useful). The magnitude gap tracks roughly linearly with TP rank count, since span generation scales with the number of ranks, and the TP=8 test used synchronous export while this one used async by default.

## Why we're filing this

- The community advice we've seen elsewhere ("lower `SGLANG_TRACE_LEVEL` to reduce overhead", "tune the async flush threshold") holds at high TP / high CPU pressure, but **doesn't transfer to smaller TP configs** — those knobs are simply inert until CPU saturates. Worth calling out in docs/guidance so users at TP<=2-4 don't spend time tuning a lever with no effect.
- The **c=50 inflection point** (throughput loss going from ~4% to ~20% within one concurrency step) suggests there may be a queueing/lock-contention effect on the trace export path that kicks in once concurrent in-flight spans cross some threshold, rather than a smooth linear cost per request. Might be worth profiling `trace_async.py`'s buffer/flush path under concurrent load to see if there's a lock or queue that serializes once request volume rises (in our TP=8 investigation, we found `trace_req_finish()`/`abort()` and `__getstate__` all trigger unconditional flushes regardless of the configured threshold, and `trace_req_start()`'s `tracer.start_span()` + `propagate.inject()` calls are synchronous OTel API calls on the request path — happy to dig further if maintainers think that's a productive direction).
- Production guidance: for small/mid TP deployments (TP<=2-4), default trace config (level=2, async on) is fine as-is. For TP=8-class deployments, overhead is materially higher and level-tuning is the effective lever — but this should probably be stated explicitly since it's not obvious from the trace docs which regime a given deployment falls into.

## Attachments

- `report-en.pdf` — full benchmark report with charts (ttft_p99 / itl_p99 / e2e_p50 / throughput vs. concurrency, delta% overview, GPU/CPU resource usage)
[Uploading report-en.pdf…]()

## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and did not find an existing report that fully covers this request shape.
- [ ] I have not re-run this on today's latest main; the reproduction was observed on pinned main commit `2f5c9ac43d76eef11e8561c89c55a79db7db715a` (2026-09-25).
- [x] Environment details and a standalone `/generate` reproducer are included below.
- [x] This is a possible correctness issue rather than a general usage question.
- [x] Report is in English.

## Describe the bug

With a hybrid GDN Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 checkpoint, repeated selected-token logprob scoring is stable when Radix Cache is disabled, but the first Radix-enabled branch scoring pass differs substantially from subsequent identical passes.

The observation is:

| Cache configuration | Max repeated selected-logprob delta | Pattern |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Unified Radix Cache enabled | `2.551527976989746` | run 1 differs; runs 2 and 3 match exactly |
| Radix Cache disabled | `0.0` | runs 1, 2 and 3 match exactly |

The prefix is explicitly warmed before the repeated branch batches. With Radix enabled, the server log reports `#cached-token: 0` for the first branch batch and `#cached-token: 128` for later identical branch batches. With Radix disabled, the three repeated branch batches are bit-stable.

This strongly correlates the drift with the cache-hit execution path, but I do **not** want to over-attribute the root cause: the current evidence does not prove that a specific GDN recurrent-state checkpoint, restore, split, or other hybrid-cache internal operation is responsible.

This was found while gating a decision workload that consumes candidate-token logprobs directly, so cache-hit equivalence matters even when the top-1 decision itself does not change.

Related work:

- #22935 — Mamba Radix cache prefix/split behavior
- #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
- #38625 — interior/no-buffer checkpoint work

I am not assuming that #22935 or #38625 has the same root cause or fully covers this request shape. In particular, I would like to know whether a shared prefix followed by divergent option branches is expected to preserve selected-token logprobs under deterministic inference when the later identical branch requests hit the hybrid cache.

## Environment

Tested environment:

- SGLang source: `2f5c9ac43d76eef11e8561c89c55a79db7db715a`
- SGLang package: `0.5.21.dev612+g2f5c9ac43`
- Model: `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-NVFP4`
- Model revision: `332d277a083ca395aa2f822842b82f5f2f3913a2`
- Architecture: `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN / full attention
- Quantization: ModelOpt mixed FP8/NVFP4
- GPUs: 2 × NVIDIA RTX 5090 (SM120), TP=2
- NVIDIA driver: `610.57.04`
- Kernel: `7.0.0-34-generic`
- Python: `3.13.11`
- PyTorch: `2.14.0a0.post20260925` (CUDA 13.4)
- Triton: `3.7.0`
- `sglang-kernel==0.4.7`
- `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b19`
- Attention backend: Triton
- Deterministic inference: enabled
- Prefill CUDA Graph: disabled
- Decode CUDA Graph: retained
- Unified Radix Cache: enabled for the failing case
- Observed Mamba strategy: `extra_buffer`
- Comparison case: identical server settings plus only `--disable-radix-cache`

A literal `python3 -m sglang.check_env` dump was not retained for this run; the exact pinned runtime versions above are from the same project environment used for the reproduction.

## Reproduction

Launch the candidate server with Radix Cache enabled:

```bash

  --model-path /path/to/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-NVFP4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp-size 2 \
```

items.title: [Bug] Hybrid-SWA + radix cache: admission livelock when the SWA prefix lock pins a finished request's untrimmed last chunk
items.author: bill-h-lin
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

With a hybrid-SWA model, the radix cache on and a tight SWA pool, the scheduler can stop admitting a request forever: 1 waiting, 0 running, GPU idle, no log line. We hit it on MiMo-V2.6-Flash (sliding window 128, page size 1) and traced it to `SWAComponent.acquire_component_lock` pinning a whole tree node that holds a finished request's untrimmed last chunk of SWA, instead of one window.

**Sequence** (`--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.06448` → SWA pool 8,451, `--context-length 131072`, `--max-running-requests 1`, overlap scheduler on):

1. A 32,768-token request with `max_new_tokens=1` (it finishes at its first token).
2. A request with the same 32,768 tokens, a different next token, then 4,999 more (37,768 in all).

Request 2 matches 32,768 cached tokens, needs 5,001 SWA slots and never runs. `/v1/loads` stayed at 1 waiting, 0 running for 43 minutes. The same sequence runs fine with `--chunked-prefill-size 4096` or with a 16,643-token SWA pool.

### Root cause (line numbers on `main` @ 6624999385)

1. Under the overlap scheduler, a request that finishes at its first token still gets one decode step prepared before its prefill result is processed: `alloc_for_decode` (`allocation.py:587`) commits one more token, and `release_kv_cache` → `insert_req(req, up_to=req.owned_kv_len())` keys `(origin_input_ids + output_ids)[:kv_committed_len]`. So it is cached with 32,769 tokens, its output token included.
2. `cleanup_after_caching_req` (`swa.py:1011`, the `not is_finished` guard at `:1023`) frees out-of-window SWA only for unfinished requests. So the request's final 8,192-token chunk keeps its SWA live. In the tree that is a node `[24,576, 32,641)` holding 8,065 live SWA slots, then the 128-token window leaf that `_maybe_split_leaf_for_swa_lock` (`swa.py:555`) capped "so locking it pins only one window".
3. Request 2 diverges at position 32,768, so its match splits the window leaf into 127 + 1. `acquire_component_lock` (`swa.py:811`) pins whole nodes until it has covered 128 tokens: the 127-token node, then the whole 8,065-token parent. **8,192 slots pinned** for a 128-token window.
4. `SWAPrefillBudget.check_prefill` (`prefill_budget.py:213`) sees 5,001 needed and 259 available. Since 5,001 fits an empty pool, it is not a permanent shortfall ("Transient pressure waits"), so the request waits for running requests to free slots. None exist.

The bound: only an untrimmed final chunk holds more than about one window of live SWA, so the lock over-pins by at most one chunk, while a request needs at most one chunk + 1. A pool of 2 × chunk + window + slack therefore always leaves enough (by 258 slots here), and one of chunk + window + slack, as above, can deadlock whenever a request reuses the path of one that finished at its first token (`max_tokens=1`, an immediate EOS or stop) and diverges inside its last window.

### Reproduction

- End to end: on a GPU (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) with SGLang at 542a043, reproduced with the sequence above. That build carries local changes (an MoE expert-offload tier, and #41263's chunked-prefill SWA free order); none of them changes the radix tree, the SWA lock or `check_prefill` (#41263 only moves when a chunked request's out-of-window SWA is freed).
- On CPU, on the same build: the same four steps, with the scheduler's own `UnifiedRadixCache`, SWA allocator and `PrefillAdder` plus the orphan decode step, give 259 / 5,001 available / needed (not admitted) at chunk 8,192 / pool 8,451, and admit at chunk 4,096 (4,355 / 4,097) and at pool 16,643 (8,451 / 5,001).
- On `main`: the unit test in the linked PR builds a live parent + capped window leaf, matches a key that diverges on the last page and locks it; the lock pins the whole parent. Links 1, 2 and 4 are unchanged in the code on `main`; we have not run the end-to-end sequence on `main`.

### Proposed fix

In the lock walk, split a live, unlocked device-SWA node that is longer than what the window still needs, so only the in-window tail is pinned (the same idea as the leaf cap, applied to whatever node the walk reaches). PR: #41580.

Related: #27210 caps compute locks by splitting the lock's endpoint node. It does not cover this case: at page size 1 the match ends inside the capped leaf, the endpoint is shorter than a window, and the over-pin comes from its parent. #32379 fixed a different SWA admission livelock (decode headroom double-counted for cached resumes).

### Environment

SGLang 542a043 (end to end) and `main` 6624999385 (unit test), CUDA 13.0, torch cu130, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm120), `--tp-size 1`, radix cache on, overlap scheduler on.

items.title: [Bug][KV Cache] nvfp4 KV silently reuses the checkpoint's fp8-calibrated k/v_scale as NVFP4 global scale → deterministic long-context corruption (single-variable proof, sm_120)
items.author: chengye75-star
items.body_excerpt:
## TL;DR

Serving an NVFP4 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`) on a checkpoint whose `quantization_config.kv_cache_scheme` says `num_bits: 8` (e.g. unsloth's NVFP4 quants, which ship fp8-calibrated `k_scale`/`v_scale`) silently corrupts the KV cache: 32 tiny `[1]` bf16 scalars are loaded verbatim and consumed as the NVFP4 **global scale**. Removing exactly those 64 **bytes** flips long-context needle from 1/4 to 4/4 on an otherwise bit-identical 22.5 GB checkpoint. No log line ever mentions scales. Related but distinct: [#36121](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36121) (fp4 scales not traveling through HiCache host transfers; footnote has our hybrid-path measurement), [#39942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39942) (fp8 KV scales silently *dropped* — opposite failure, same blind spot: nothing validates KV scale provenance).

## Setup

SGLang 0.5.21 (official PyPI wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120, TP2), driver 595.91.07. Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid 16 full-attention + 48 GDN layers, head_dim 256, compressed-tensors). Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --prefill-attention-backend flashinfer --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --context-length 195000 --page-size 64`, greedy, chat format. (Same rig as my [#36010 evidence post](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36010#issuecomment-5788493111); this bug is **independent of spec decode** — it hits the plain no-spec nvfp4 path.)

## Symptom

With scales as shipped, long-context retrieval collapses: needle **1/4 (d50) / 0/4 (d500)**; answers degenerate into question-echoing after a short thinking block. Everything else looks healthy — boot logs clean, short prompts / tool calls / vision normal. Deterministic: completion tokens reproduce byte-for-byte across boots and repeats.

## Root cause (source walk; mechanism marked as inference)

1. The checkpoint carries 32 per-layer `*.self_attn.{k,v}_scale` tensors — `[1]` bf16 scalars calibrated for **fp8** KV (`config.json → kv_cache_scheme: {num_bits: 8, static_minmax, symmetric}`).
2. *(inference, from source)* At load, `weight_utils.maybe_remap_kv_scale_name()` attaches them to the attention modules unconditionally; the fp4 path (`layers/attention/kvfp4_tensor.py`, comment: *"The KV cache path passes preloaded per-layer scales already on device"*) consumes them as the NVFP4 `global_scale` in `x_fp4 * block_scale * global_scale`.
3. *(inference)* Nothing validates the checkpoint's KV scheme against the runtime `--kv-cache-dtype`. An fp8-geometry scalar (amax/448 family) applied under NVFP4 geometry (amax/6 family) is off by ~75× → every stored K/V is systematically mis-scaled.

## Single-variable proof (same box, same day, same prompts)

| config (one variable per row) | needle d50 | needle d500 |
|---|---|---|
| unsloth + nvfp4, scales as shipped | 1/4 | 0/4 |
| **unsloth + nvfp4, 32 scale tensors stripped (64 bytes total), `kv_cache_scheme=null`** | **4/4** | **4/4** |
| unsloth + fp8_e4m3 (scale geometry matches dtype) | 4/4 | 2/4 |
| `sakamakismile/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-NVFP4` + nvfp4 (checkpoint ships no scales) | 4/4 | 1/4 |

The stripped copy is a hardlink farm with only `model.safetensors` rewritten (header offsets recomputed; post-check: 0 leftover scale tensors) — the rest of the ~22.5 GB is byte-identical. Same-checkpoint before/after is the control: 64 bytes of metadata move the score by three needle questions.

## Why this is not an edge case

The filename pairing (`…-NVFP4` weights + `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`) is the natural reading, and unsloth's NVFP4 releases ship fp8-calibrated KV scales as a matter of their recipe. Everyone doing that pairing gets silently wrong KV with zero log evidence; needle-style evals are the only thing that notices, and most people don't run those. Checkpoints without shipped scales (dynamic path, row 4) are unaffected — which is presumably why this hasn't surfaced loudly.

## Asks

1. **Validate at load**: if the checkpoint carries `k_scale`/`v_scale` and `kv_cache_scheme.num_bits` disagrees with `server_args.kv_cache_dtype`, warn loudly and skip them (fall back to dynamic scales) instead of reinterpreting an fp8 scalar as an fp4 global scale.
2. Checkpoints whose scheme says `num_bits: 4` (e.g. NVIDIA/ModelOpt NVFP4-KV exports) *should* consume their scales — the bug is specifically the mismatched pair, not scale loading per se.
3. Optional `--load-kv-scales {auto,never}` for quick A/B without safetensors surgery (our workaround rewrites a 22 GB file's header — works in 3 minutes, but terrifying to recommend).

## Verified workaround & production numbers

Drop the 32 `*.self_attn.[kv]_scale` tensors from `model.safetensors`, rewrite header offsets, set `quantization_config.kv_cache_scheme = null`. The healthy config now serves our production: 185K-token cold prefill ~176 s, decode ~25 tok/s; with HiCache L2 (20 GB host, `write_through`, `page_first`, slru) a post-eviction 185K re-ask lands in **2.4–5.5 s** (vs 178 s cold) with the secret code word intact across the L2 round-trip (2/2 rounds, backup counters confirm real transfers); needle 4/4+4/4; tool-calls live. sm_120 hybrid-attention reference points are thin here — happy to post logs/transcripts.

Footnote re #36121: its fail-fast covers paths our hybrid assembly doesn't traverse (UnifiedRadixCache picks host pools in `hybrid_pool_assembler`), and in our exact combo (nvfp4 + HiCache + page_first + write_through) the fp4 block scales evidently *do* survive L2 as measured above — so the guard as drafted wouldn't cover this configuration either way. Full hybrid-path measurements posted as a review note on that PR.

items.author: nvpohanh
items.body_excerpt:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- sglang-flaky-tracker:v1 -->

This issue tracks **flaky tests** and **recurring CI infrastructure failures** seen in NVIDIA `PR Test Base` / `PR Test Extra` runs while babysitting PRs with the `/sglang-pr-babysit` Claude Code workflow. It complements the CI tracker #17050. #17050 lists every failure signature by date. This issue records one row per flaky test, how often it was hit, and whether a rerun with no code change passed. Use it to pick the flakiest tests to debug.

A row is added only when triage found concrete evidence that the failure is **not caused by the PR** and **not a breakage on `main`**. PR-caused failures, `main` breakages, and uncertain cases are left out.

## Flaky tests

| ID | Test | Signature | Runner | Seen | Rerun passed | First seen | Last seen | Recent jobs | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `test/registered/lora/test_multi_lora_backend.py::TestMultiLoRABackend::test_ci_lora_models_multi_batch` | `AssertionError: ROUGE-L score <N> below tolerance 1.0` | `1-gpu-h100` | 5 | 4/5 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | [#41593](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454554618/job/112366109419), [#34535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37472718685/job/112319479525), [#33395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454576286/job/112248674725) | open |
| T5 | `test/registered/e2e/models/test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_h200.py::TestDSV4FlashFP4H200FlashInferCutlass::test_bs_1_speed` | `AssertionError: <N> not greater than 2.8` | `8-gpu-h200` | 2 | 1/2 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-07 | [#34535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37472718685/job/112592256344), [#34535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37472718685/job/112465283691) | open |
| T2 | `test/registered/core/test_basic_sanity.py` | `Run test step timed out after <N> minutes with no test output` | `1-gpu-5090` | 1 | 1/1 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | [#34535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37472718685/job/112300624953) | open |
| T3 | `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_storage.py` | `Run test step timed out after <N> minutes; file ran <N>s vs estimated <N>s` | `1-gpu-5090` | 1 | 1/1 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | [#36810](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454162206/job/112246794195) | open |
| T4 | `test/registered/e2e/models/test_glm53_flash_b200.py::TestGLM53FlashB200LowLatency::test_gsm8k` | `AssertionError: np.float64(<N>) not greater than or equal to 0.93` | `4-gpu-b200` | 1 | 1/1 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | [#33395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454576286/job/112428464909) | open |

## CI infrastructure failures

| ID | Job / step | Signature | Runner | Seen | Rerun passed | First seen | Last seen | Recent jobs | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | `wait-for-base-b` / `wait-for-jobs` | `RequestError [HttpError]: Server Error` (GitHub jobs API 5xx) | `ubuntu-latest` | 4 | 2/4 | 2026-10-05 | 2026-10-06 | [#33395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454576286/job/112388430204), [#33395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37454576286/job/112248674181), [#42022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37302243358/job/111853982288) | open |

## Format (v1)

Each row is one failure mode, keyed by **Test** (or **Job / step**) plus **Signature**. The same test failing with a different signature gets its own row.

- **ID**: `T<n>` for tests and `I<n>` for infra. IDs are never reused, even when a row is fixed.
- **Test**: `path::Class::method`, with the path relative to the repo root. Use `path` alone if the method is unknown.
- **Job / step**: the workflow job name, a slash, and the failing step or action.
- **Signature**: the exception type and message, with run-specific values (numbers, paths, hashes, ports, timestamps) replaced by `<N>`, `<PATH>`, and so on. At most about 100 characters.
- **Runner**: the runner label of the failing job, for example `1-gpu-h100` or `8-gpu-b300`.
- **Seen**: the number of failed job attempts recorded. Each failed attempt counts once, including a failed rerun.
- **Rerun passed**: `P/R`. `R` is the number of occurrences whose rerun has finished. `P` is how many of those reruns passed the same job with no code change.
- **First seen** / **Last seen**: UTC dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Recent jobs**: links to the last 3 failing jobs, newest first. Each link is labeled with its PR number.
- **Status**: `open`; `investigating (@user or #issue)`; or `fixed (#PR)`. If a `fixed` row fails again after the fix merged, it returns to `open` with `regressed after #PR`.

Rows are sorted by **Seen**, highest first. Ties are broken by **Last seen**, newest first.

Every occurrence is also posted as a comment on this issue. The comment starts with `<!-- sglang-flaky-occurrence:v1 -->` and holds the entry ID, PR, job link, why the failure is unrelated to the PR, and the rerun result. The comments are the append-only record, and the tables above are their summary.

## For debugging agents

Start from the top of each table. A test row with a high **Seen** count and a high **Rerun passed** ratio is a confirmed flake, and it is worth fixing or stabilizing. When you take a row, set its **Status** to `investigating (@you)`. When the fix merges, set it to `fixed (#PR)`.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-27B compressed-tensors W4A16 (int4, symmetric, group 128) serves with degraded quality on 0.5.19-0.5.21 (wikitext PPL 9.98 vs 6.05 on vLLM, same checkpoint)
items.author: jolpindo96
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. (Related, but different code path: #41835 is about `AutoRoundConfig`; this checkpoint loads through `CompressedTensorsConfig`.)
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound` is a compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` checkpoint: one config group targeting `Linear`, 4-bit, `symmetric: true`, `group_size: 128`, no actorder. SGLang loads and serves it with no errors or warnings, but the output distribution is far from the model's. vLLM serves the same files correctly.

I measured it with prompt logprobs on wikitext-2 test: 20 chunks of 2048 tokens, scoring the last 1023 tokens of each chunk (20,460 positions), top-2000 logprobs per position, with the same token ids sent to every engine. The reference is a llama.cpp Q8_0 GGUF of the same model (PPL 6.0539). KLD is a lower bound computed from the top-2000 lists (tokens outside them pooled into one bucket on both sides).

| Engine (same checkpoint) | PPL | KLD vs reference | Top-1 agreement |
|---|---|---|---|
| SGLang 0.5.19 | 9.6276 | - | 70.2% |
| SGLang 0.5.20 | 9.7036 | 0.554 | 69.8% |
| SGLang 0.5.21 | 9.9767 | 0.590 | 69.1% |
| vLLM 0.30.0 | 6.0528 | 0.042 | 92.9% |

- This is not a precision issue. SGLang 0.5.20 and 0.5.21 disagree with each other (KL 0.42, top-1 73%) about as much as each disagrees with the reference. That looks like structurally wrong weights or a wrong transform, and the output changes whenever the kernels change.
- An asymmetric int4 checkpoint of the same model, `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4` (group 32), was correct on 0.5.19 (PPL 6.0699, top-1 93.4%).
- The harness is stable. On the same machine, an NVFP4 checkpoint of this model reproduced the same PPL (6.5007) and KLD estimate to every printed digit on 0.5.19 and 0.5.20.
- The checkpoint leaves 215 modules unquantized: the vision tower, `linear_attn.in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b` in all 48 GatedDeltaNet layers, `lm_head`, and the MTP layers.

**What I ruled out.** SGLang fuses `in_proj_b` + `in_proj_a` into `in_proj_ba`, and `in_proj_qkv` + `in_proj_z` into `in_proj_qkvz`. The text model is built under the prefix `model.language_model`, which matches the checkpoint's ignore entries. In the 0.5.21 image, `should_ignore_layer("model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_ba", ignore=<checkpoint ignore list>, fused_mapping=Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping)` returns `True`, so the bf16 gating projections should load unquantized.

**Remaining suspects (not verified):**
- loading the packed int4 `in_proj_qkv` into three shards of the fused `in_proj_qkvz` (stacked mapping `("in_proj_qkvz.", "in_proj_qkv.", (0, 1, 2))`);
- the symmetric group-128 WNA16 kernel path.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 30000:30000 -v hf-cache:/root/.cache lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130 \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --context-length 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --disable-radix-cache --trust-remote-code \
  --max-running-requests 4 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Send one request per 2048-token chunk:

```json
POST /generate
{"input_ids": [2048 wikitext-2 token ids],
 "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0},
 "return_logprob": true, "logprob_start_len": 0, "top_logprobs_num": 2000}
```

PPL = exp(mean negative `input_token_logprobs` over the last 1023 tokens of each chunk). The vLLM control sends the same token ids to `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs`. The 0.5.19 run used different flags (32k context, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `--max-running-requests 8`) and failed the same way. I can share the scoring script.

### Environment

From `python3 -m sglang.check_env` in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130`:

```
Python: 3.12.3
GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, Compute Capability 12.0
CUDA Driver Version: 616.92
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: 0.5.21
sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.12.1
Hypervisor vendor: Microsoft (Windows 11 host, Docker Desktop / WSL2)
```

Only tested on sm_120.

*Disclosure: an AI assistant (Claude) helped build the scoring harness, run the measurements and draft this report; I reviewed it and can re-run any of it.*

items.title: FlashInfer autotune for trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe wedges forever on SM103 (GB300): trtllm_gemm cubin is sm_100a-only, no PTX, and the autotuner has no timeout
items.author: ebfio
items.body_excerpt:
> **EDIT (2026-09-23):** The root-cause attribution below is **withdrawn**. `nm -D` shows the `fp4_block_scale_moe` symbols live in `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100.so` (which carries `sm_103a` cubins), not `trtllm_gemm.so` (the dense GEMM module — the sm_100a-only observation is real but irrelevant to this op). The "candidate can never execute on SM103" mechanism does not hold. The symptom stands (unbounded autotune at boot, 40+ min, zero progress lines, no cache write before termination); it is now considered a probable extreme-slow-crawl rather than a proven hang, since the autotuner logs nothing between start and end and only writes the cache on completion. See [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58031#issuecomment-5788562400) for the corrected analysis and proposed scoping (exclude SM103 from `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` auto-selection; add per-bucket progress logging). The workaround below remains valid.

## Describe the bug

On a DGX Station GB300 (SM103, compute capability 10.3), the FlashInfer autotune for `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` runs indefinitely at 100% GPU with zero progress and zero autotune cache writes, wedging engine startup forever. There is no error, no traceback, no timeout — the boot simply never completes.

The root cause appears to be an arch-coverage gap in FlashInfer's prebuilt `trtllm_gemm` cubin, combined with an autotuner that has no timeout for a candidate kernel that never terminates.

## Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` pulled 2026-09-21 (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev452+g3df4ae153`, FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1`), arm64
- GPU: NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), driver 610.43.02
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 experts / MXFP8 rest), TP1, `--cpu-offload-gb 75`, DSpark speculative k=5
- Flags relevant: `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, moe backend auto-selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`

## Reproduction

Serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (or any model that routes MoE through `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) on SM103 **without** skipping the op's autotune. Boot proceeds normally through weight load, CUDA graph capture, and JIT warmup, then reaches:

```
[flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:267] Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
[kernel_warmup.py:436] Using FlashInfer autotune cache file: .../autotune_configs.json
autotuner.py:972 - flashinfer.jit: [Autotuner]: Autotuning process starts ...
[kernel_warmup.py:358] Running FlashInfer autotune with 16384 tokens and token buckets (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536, 1792, 2048, 2560, 3072, 3584, 4096, 8192, 16384).
```

… and stays there. Observed: 40+ minutes at 100% GPU utilization, 0 new log lines in any 10-minute window, and the cache directory for the config hash created but left **empty**:

```
drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Sep 21 15:35 .   # created when autotune started
# (no autotune_configs.json ever written)
```

By contrast, the JIT kernel warmup immediately before it completes with per-batch progress lines (10/10 batches in 47s), so the wedge is specific to this op's autotune, not to warmup in general.

The same behavior existed on the launch-day `deepseekv41-flash-0909` image, which is why this deployment has carried `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS="trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe,flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe"` since September 9. Reproducing it on current nightly shows the gap is not fixed.

## Root cause evidence

Inspecting FlashInfer's prebuilt cubins in the nightly image (`flashinfer_jit_cache`):

```console
# 907 .so files in flashinfer_jit_cache overall — sm_103a coverage exists:
$ for so in $(find . -name "*.so"); do cuobjdump -lelf $so 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "sm_103[a-z]?"; done | sort | uniq -c
   3380 sm_103a

# …but the cubin the fp4 block-scale MoE autotuner benchmarks:
$ cuobjdump -lelf .../jit_cache/trtllm_gemm/trtllm_gemm.so | grep -oE "sm_[0-9]+[a-z]?" | sort | uniq -c
      1 sm_100a

$ cuobjdump -ptx .../jit_cache/trtllm_gemm/trtllm_gemm.so | grep -oE "target sm_[0-9]+" | sort | uniq -c
      (empty — no PTX section at all)
```

`trtllm_gemm.so` ships **only an `sm_100a` cubin and no PTX**. An arch-specific (`a`-suffixed) cubin runs on exactly its target arch and never on a later one (this is the same mechanism as the `cooperative_topk` SM103 gap documented in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SM103 patch work — `sm_100a` cubins are unusable on SM103, and without PTX there is nothing to JIT forward).

So on SM103 the autotuner launches a candidate that either fails its launch silently or spins in a grid-stride loop sized for a different arch, and the `cudaEventSynchronize` in the timing loop blocks forever. The autotuner has no per-candidate timeout, so one non-terminating candidate wedges the whole boot.

## Suggested fixes (either would do; both would be robust)

1. **Ship an `sm_103a` (and ideally `sm_103`-JITable PTX) build of `trtllm_gemm`** — the rest of the JIT cache clearly builds for 103a (3,380 cubins), so this specific module looks like an omission rather than a fundamental limitation.
2. **Add a timeout to the FlashInfer autotuner per candidate/bucket** — a wedged candidate should be skipped and logged, not hang the engine forever. Right now one bad kernel costs an unbounded boot.

## Workaround

```
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS="trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe,flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe"
```

With the skip, the same configuration boots to serving in ~8 minutes; the op then runs on its default (untuned) kernel selection. Measured decode on this deployment is ~91 tok/s single-stream with the skip in place.

## Additional context

- Full deployment config and the SM103 patch history: https://github.com/ebfio/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gb300
- The engine does not log *which* candidate config it was benchmarking when it wedged — if maintainers want a `py-spy dump` from a wedged process or a CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING run, I can reproduce the wedge on demand and capture it.

items.title: [Bug] DFlash2/DSpark + prefix caching corrupt output after a cache hit on Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (compressed-tensors) on 0.30/0.31; 0.29, FP8 target and MTP are fine
items.author: sinmkd
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.31.0 (also reproduced on 0.30.0). vLLM 0.29.0 passes the same test.
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python/cubin 0.7.0.post1 (0.6.18.post1 on 0.30.0), CUDA 13.3, driver 610.57.04
- 1× RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 48 GB (sm_120), Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-34
- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` NVFP4 checkpoint, compressed-tensors mixed precision (NVFP4 on the MLP projections, FP8 W8A8 on attention / GDN projections / lm_head, `linear_attn.{in_proj_a,in_proj_b,norm}` and `mtp.*` unquantized via `ignore`)
- Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`DFlash2DraftModel`, sliding_window 2048), `num_speculative_tokens: 7`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Since 0.30.0, serving Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 with the DFlash2 drafter and prefix caching enabled produces garbage after a prefix-cache hit. The first requests of a conversation are fine. From the third request on, once the prompt resumes from cached blocks, the model emits a single repeated token (`duct`, over and over) with no coherent content, and the drafter accepts nothing (`SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted: 0 tokens`). The same five requests against 0.29.0 come back coherent every time. I have run the comparison twice on each version.

The test is a replay of a real agent conversation: five consecutive chat-completions requests from one session (31,776 / 45,606 / 52,737 / 65,364 / 67,502 prompt tokens, 25 tool schemas, seed 17), sent in order to a fresh engine so each request hits the previous one's prefix. The conversation itself is private, but I can build a synthetic equivalent if that helps.

Serve command (production flags):

```
vllm serve /models/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 250000 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 17379961324 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":20,"min_p":0.0}' --scheduling-policy priority
```

env: `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`. Prefix caching on (default), `mamba_cache_mode` resolves to `align`.

### What I tried, to narrow it down

All on 0.31.0, same five requests, fresh engine each time:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing (command above) | fails at request 3 |
| PR #57128 applied (the `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` / `drop_eagle_block` fix) | fails |
| `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` instead of FlashInfer | fails |
| `--linear-backend cutlass` (in-tree CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM) | fails |
| `--linear-backend marlin` (weight-only W4A16, no activation quant) | fails |
| smaller KV pool / 180K window / util 0.94 (copied from my FP8 route) | fails |
| `"disable_eagle_block_drop": true` in the speculative config | worse: garbage from request 1, even cold |
| **no speculative config at all** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (checkpoint's own MTP head)** | **passes 5/5** |
| **`{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}`** | **fails at request 3** |
| **FP8 target (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `quant_method: fp8`) with the same DFlash2 config** | **passes 5/5, twice** |

A unique `cache_salt` per request on 0.30.0 also makes requests 3–5 pass, so the failure needs an actual cache hit.

So the NVFP4 GEMM kernels are not involved (three different kernels, including weight-only, all fail), the GDN prefill kernel is not involved, and the KV pool size is not involved. What it needs is: a hidden-state drafter (DFlash2 or DSpark; MTP is fine) + a prefix-cache hit + this compressed-tensors NVFP4 target, on 0.30 or later. The FP8 checkpoint with the identical drafter config is fine. Turning off the EAGLE trailing-block drop makes it strictly worse, which reads to me like the drafter is leaving bad Mamba/GDN state in the cached tail block and the drop normally hides it inside a request but not across requests.

The compressed-tensors checkpoint is the obvious difference from the FP8 one: it has an `ignore` list covering `linear_attn` sub-modules (the bf16 `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b` / `norm`) alongside `config_groups` that target `linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,out_proj}` at FP8. If the drafter path resolves those layers differently from the plain `fp8` loader, that would be where I'd look first, but I haven't gone further than the table above.

Related: #53912 and #55766 describe neighbouring hybrid-GDN prefix-cache corruption with speculative decoding.

### What I can provide

Per-request replay output (prompt token counts, finish reasons, draft metrics), engine logs for every ablation above, and a synthetic reproducer on request.

items.title: [Feature] L1/L2/L3 cache hit rate observability — Prometheus metrics, OTel spans & per-request JSONL trace
items.author: grissomsh
items.body_excerpt:
### Motivation

LMCache's current `PrometheusLogger` provides basic metrics (`time_to_retrieve`, `num_retrieve_requests`), but is missing:

1. **Per-tier cache hit rate** — no way to distinguish whether a hit came from L2 (CPU RAM), L3 (NVMe Disk), or a remote backend.
2. **TTFT decomposition** — `frontend_latency` (API server → engine core) and per-request `kv_lookup_time` / `kv_retrieve_time` are not surfaced.
3. **Per-request tracing** — no way to correlate cache-hit details to an individual request for debugging latency spikes.

These gaps make it hard to answer operational questions like: *"Why did TTFT spike — was it a slow disk read, CPU cache contention, or GPU prefix cache eviction?"*

---

### Design Goals

1. **Three-layer observability model**: throughput → latency → cache hit rate
2. **Minimally invasive**: extend existing `LMCStatsMonitor`, `PrometheusLogger`, and `cache_engine` — no breaking API changes
3. **TP-aware**: cross-process bridge via `/dev/shm` for Worker ↔ EngineCore per-request data relay when TP > 1
4. **Self-verifying**: every trace carries token identity equations for automated correctness validation

---

### Proposed Design

#### Layer 1 — Throughput: Token Source Decomposition

```
Tokens/s = local_compute + L1_hit + L2_hit + L3_hit + remote_hit
```

**Approach**: Extend `cache_engine.py`'s `retrieve()` / `retrieve_layer()` to classify hit tokens by storage backend. Add a `_BACKEND_NAME_TO_HIT_TIER` mapping:

| Backend | Tier |
|---------|------|
| `LocalCPUBackend` | L2 |
| `LocalDiskBackend` / `GdsBackend` | L3 |
| `RemoteBackend` | Remote |

**New Prometheus metrics** (6 total):

| Metric | Type |
|--------|------|
| `lmcache:l2_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_l2_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |
| `lmcache:l3_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_l3_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |
| `lmcache:remote_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_remote_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |

#### Layer 2 — Latency: TTFT Decomposition

```
TTFT = frontend_latency + queue_time + prefill_time
prefill_time ⊃ kv_lookup_time + kv_retrieve_time
```

**Approach**: Add `LMCacheKVConnectorStats` (extending vLLM's `KVConnectorStats`) on the vLLM side, and expose per-request timing through `vllm_v1_adapter.py`'s `request_finished()` via `EngineCoreOutput.kv_transfer_params`.

**New Prometheus metrics** (9 bridge metrics + 1 framework metric):

| Metric | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `vllm:lmcache_kv_lookup_seconds` | Histogram | KV lookup latency |
| `vllm:lmcache_kv_retrieve_seconds` | Histogram | KV retrieve latency |
| `vllm:lmcache_retrieve_process_tokens_seconds` | Histogram | Retrieve: process_tokens phase |
| `vllm:lmcache_retrieve_to_gpu_seconds` | Histogram | Retrieve: CPU→GPU DMA phase |
| `vllm:lmcache_num_l2_hit_tokens` | Counter | vLLM-side L2 bridge |
| `vllm:lmcache_num_l3_hit_tokens` | Counter | vLLM-side L3 bridge |
| `vllm:lmcache_num_remote_hit_tokens` | Counter | vLLM-side remote bridge |
| `vllm:request_frontend_latency_seconds` | Histogram | API server → engine core latency |

#### Layer 3 — Cache Hit Rate & Per-Request Trace

One JSONL `[trace]` line emitted per request at completion:

```json
{
  "ts": 1782023561.679,
  "rid": "chatcmpl-xxx",
  "prompt_tokens": 3934,
  "output_tokens": 32,
  "TTFT_ms": 169.2,
  "queue_ms": 0.04,
  "prefill_ms": 130.1,
  "decode_ms": 144.6,
  "e2e_ms": 314.3,
  "frontend_ms": 39.0,
  "input_tokens_cache_hit": 3840,
  "L1_hit": 0,
  "external_kv_hit": 3840,
  "L2_hit": 0,
  "L3_hit": 3840,
  "remote_hit": 0,
  "input_tokens_no_cache_hit": 94,
  "kv_transfer_mode": "non_layerwise",
  "kv_lookup_ms": 1.2,
  "kv_retrieve_ms": 101.5
}
```

**Token identity equations** (verifiable by automated scripts at runtime):

```
prompt_tokens = input_tokens_cache_hit + input_tokens_no_cache_hit
input_tokens_cache_hit = L1_hit + external_kv_hit
external_kv_hit ≈ L2_hit + L3_hit + remote_hit   (≈ due to chunk_size=256 granularity)
```

#### Cross-Process Bridge (TP > 1)

When TP > 1, `retrieve()` runs on Worker_TP0 while `request_finished()` runs on the EngineCore/scheduler process. Per-request data is relayed via file-based bridge in `/dev/shm/lmcache_bridge/` (tmpfs, memory-backed):

- Per-tier counters: file + `fcntl.flock` for atomic cross-process updates
- Timing data: `write-tmp + os.replace` for atomic JSON
- Cleanup: throttled periodic sweep + retry limit (3) to prevent `/dev/shm` exhaustion

#### OTel Span Attributes

8 attributes on the `"llm_request"` span:

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `gen_ai.latency.time_in_frontend` | API → engine |
| `gen_ai.latency.time_in_kv_lookup` | KV lookup |
| `gen_ai.latency.time_in_kv_transfer` | KV retrieve |
| `gen_ai.usage.l1_hit_tokens` | L1 (GPU prefix cache) |
| `gen_ai.usage.l2_hit_tokens` | L2 (CPU RAM) |
| `gen_ai.usage.l3_hit_tokens` | L3 (NVMe/SSD) |
| `gen_ai.usage.remote_hit_tokens` | Remote backend |
| `gen_ai.latency.kv_transfer_mode` | layerwise / non_layerwise |

---

### Metrics Summary (16 new Prometheus metrics)

**LMCache side (6):**

| Metric | Type |
|--------|------|
| `lmcache:l2_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_l2_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |
| `lmcache:l3_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_l3_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |
| `lmcache:remote_hit_tokens` / `lmcache:num_remote_hit_tokens` | Histogram + Counter |

**vLLM bridge (9):**

| Metric | Type |
|--------|------|
| `vllm:lmcache_kv_lookup_seconds` | Histogram |
| `vllm:lmcache_kv_retrieve_seconds` | Histogram |
